title.zh: 卷八十下 文苑列傳
title.raw: 卷八十下 文苑列傳 Volume 80b: Biographies of Writers 2

sentences.zh: 张升字彦真，陈留尉氏人，富平侯放之孙也。

translations.literal: Zhang Sheng, courtesy name Yanzhen, was a native of Weishi in Chenliu and grandson of Marquis of Fuping Fang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Sheng, styled Yanzhen, came from Weishi in Chenliu and was the grandson of Fang, Marquis of Fuping.

sentences.zh: 升少好学，多关览，而任情不羁。

translations.literal: In youth he loved learning, read broadly, and indulged his temperament without restraint.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he devoured books and wandered wherever impulse led him.

sentences.zh: 其意相合者，则倾身交结，不问穷贱；

translations.literal: When minds matched he threw himself into friendship and never asked whether men were poor or base.
translations.idiomatic: Kindred spirits won his whole heart—rank never entered the reckoning.

sentences.zh: 如乖真志好者，虽王公大人，终不屈从。

translations.literal: When tastes diverged, though facing kings and dukes he never bent.
translations.idiomatic: Where conscience pointed elsewhere he would not yield even to royalty.

sentences.zh: 常叹曰：“死生有命，富贵在天。

translations.literal: He often sighed: "Death and life have their allotted span; wealth and honor lie with Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: He liked to say life and death are fated and fortune hangs on Heaven.

sentences.zh: 其有知我，虽胡越可亲；

translations.literal: "Those who understand me—even Hu and Yue may draw near."
translations.idiomatic: Find a kindred soul and barbarians beyond the frontier feel like kin.

sentences.zh: 苟不相识，从物何益？”

translations.literal: "If they do not understand me—what good come from mere goods?"
translations.idiomatic: Without recognition stuff piles up for nothing.

sentences.zh: 仕郡为纲纪，以能出守外黄令。

translations.literal: He served his commandery as chief clerk and for competence was posted magistrate of Waihuang.
translations.idiomatic: From commandery registrar his talent earned him the magistracy of Waihuang.

sentences.zh: 吏有受賕者，即論殺之。

translations.literal: When clerks took bribes he tried and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: Bribe-taking clerks went straight from trial to execution.

sentences.zh: 或譏：「升守領一時，何足趨明威戮乎？」

translations.literal: Some mocked: "You governed only a short while—why hurry to awe-inspiring executions?"
translations.idiomatic: Critics sneered that a brief tenure hardly justified bloody severity.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「昔仲尼暫相，誅齊之侏儒，手足異門而出，故能威震強國，反其侵地。

translations.literal: He replied: "Anciently Confucius briefly served as minister and executed Qi State's dwarf performers—limbs shipped out separate gates—thereby awe shook a strong land and recovered invaded soil."
translations.idiomatic: He quoted Confucius's stint in Lu: one decisive stroke against ridicule cowed a great power and won back stolen ground.

sentences.zh: 君子仕不爲己，職思其憂，豈以久近而異其度哉？」

translations.literal: "The gentleman holds office not for private gain but bears its cares in mind—how could term length alter his measure?"
translations.idiomatic: The nobleman serves the burden of office, not its perks—duration cannot change the moral yardstick.

sentences.zh: 遇黨錮去官，後竟見誅，年四十九。

translations.literal: He lost office in the Party Prohibition and was eventually executed—aged forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: The faction purge stripped him of rank; he was killed later at forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 著賊、誄、頌、碑、書，凡六十篇。

translations.literal: His writings include fu, dirges, hymns, stele texts, and letters—sixty pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Sixty works survive: fu, laments, songs, inscriptions, and letters.

sentences.zh: 赵壹字元叔，汉阳西县人也。

translations.literal: Zhao Yi, courtesy name Yuanshu, was a native of Xixian in Hanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yi, called Yuanshu, hailed from Xixian in Hanyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 體貌魁梧，身長九尺，美須豪眉，望之甚偉。

translations.literal: His frame was imposing—nine chi tall—with handsome beard and bold brows; he looked magnificent.
translations.idiomatic: He stood nine chi, broad-shouldered, with a splendid beard and stern brows—every inch the hero.

sentences.zh: 而恃才倨傲，爲鄉黨所擯，乃作《解擯》。

translations.literal: Yet relying on his talent he was arrogant, was ostracized by his village community, and so wrote “Dispelling Ostracism.”
translations.idiomatic: Talent made him proud; his neighbors shunned him, so he wrote “Dispelling Ostracism.”

sentences.zh: 後屢抵罪，幾至死，友人救，得免。

translations.literal: Later he repeatedly offended the law and nearly died; friends rescued him.
translations.idiomatic: Further brushes with the courts nearly cost his life until friends paid him free.

sentences.zh: 壹乃貽書謝恩曰：昔原大夫贖桑下絶氣，傳稱其仁；

translations.literal: Yi then sent a letter thanking the favor, saying: “In the past, the Yuan grandee redeemed the man whose breath was failing beneath the mulberry; the tradition praises his humanity.”
translations.idiomatic: Yi wrote back in thanks: “Long ago, the grandee Yuan ransomed a dying man beneath a mulberry, and tradition praised his kindness.”

sentences.zh: 秦越人還虢太子結脈，世著其神。

translations.literal: Qin Yueren restored the pulse of Guo's crown prince—the age celebrated his spirit-like skill.
translations.idiomatic: The physician Bian Que revived Guo's heir—the world marveled at his touch.

sentences.zh: 設曩之二人不遭仁遇神，則結絶之氣竭矣。

translations.literal: Had those two men not encountered humane aid and divine skill, the breath already cut would have been exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Without such mercy and healing the last breath would have fled.

sentences.zh: 然而糒脯出乎車軨，針石運乎手爪。

translations.literal: Yet dried provisions and meat came forth from the carriage box, and needles and stones were moved by hands and fingers.
translations.idiomatic: Yet aid came as dried provisions from a carriage box and healing needles guided by human hands.

sentences.zh: 今所賴者，非直車軨之糒脯，手爪之針石也。

translations.literal: What we rely on today is not merely dried meat from the shaft-ring or needles from fingertips.
translations.idiomatic: My debt today is no mere snack from a cart or prick of a needle.

sentences.zh: 乃收之於斗極，還之於司命，使乾皮復含血，枯骨復被肉，允所謂遭仁遇神，眞所宜傳而著之。

translations.literal: You gathered me from the Dipper's pivot and returned me to the Director of Fates—making dry hide ooze blood again and bare bone grow flesh—truly meeting kindness and spirit skill—worthy of transmission and fame.
translations.idiomatic: You pulled me from the Pole Star's vault and handed me back to the Lord of Fate until parchment skin bled again and bare bones wore flesh—such rescue deserves songs.

sentences.zh: 餘畏禁，不敢班班顯言，竊爲《窮鳥賦》一篇。

translations.literal: I fear prohibition and dare not speak openly—privately I composed one piece 《Fu on the Destitute Bird》.
translations.idiomatic: Forbidden to speak plainly, I hid my thanks inside 《Fu on the Destitute Bird》.

sentences.zh: 其辭曰：有一窮鳥，戢翼原野。

translations.literal: Its words said: “There was a distressed bird, folding its wings in the open fields.”
translations.idiomatic: It began: “A trapped bird folded its wings in the wilds.”

sentences.zh: 畢網加上，機穽在下，前見蒼隼，後見驅者，繳彈張右，羿子彀左，飛丸激矢，交集於我。

translations.literal: Nets were added above and trigger-pits lay below; ahead appeared a goshawk, behind appeared the drivers; pellet-cords were drawn on the right and Yi’s bow was bent on the left, so flying pellets and swift arrows converged upon me.
translations.idiomatic: Nets closed overhead and hidden traps waited below; hawks were before me, beaters behind me, slings to the right and bows to the left, until stones and arrows converged from every side.

sentences.zh: 思飛不得，欲鳴不可，舉頭畏觸，搖足恐墮。

translations.literal: It thought of flying but could not; it wished to cry out but could not. Raising its head, it feared striking something; moving its feet, it feared falling.
translations.idiomatic: Flight was impossible and song forbidden; every lift of the head risked collision, every shift of the feet a fall.

sentences.zh: 内独怖急，乍冰乍火。

translations.literal: Inwardly it trembled between ice and fire.
translations.idiomatic: Inside it shivered and burned by turns.

sentences.zh: 幸賴大賢，我矜我憐，昔濟我南，今振我西。

translations.literal: Luckily great worthies pitied it—once they aided it south, now they revive it west.
translations.idiomatic: Great men pitied the creature—first shelter to the south, now rescue in the west.

sentences.zh: 鳥也雖頑，猶識密思。

translations.literal: Though dull, the bird still recognizes hidden kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Dull as the bird is, it still knows hidden grace.

sentences.zh: 內以書心，外用告天。

translations.literal: Inwardly it inscribes gratitude in writing; outwardly it announces it to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: It sets thanks within lines and calls Heaven to witness without.

sentences.zh: 天乎祚賢，歸賢永年，且公且侯，子子孫孫。

translations.literal: Heaven, bless the worthy; return long years to the worthy, making them both dukes and marquises, with sons and grandsons through the generations.
translations.idiomatic: May Heaven bless the worthy with long life, noble rank, and descendants generation after generation.

sentences.zh: 又作《刺世疾邪賦》，以舒其怨憤。

translations.literal: He also composed 《Fu Assailing the Age's Evil》 to vent resentment.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote 《Fu Assailing the Age's Evil》 to purge his rage.

sentences.zh: 曰：伊五帝之不同禮，三王亦又不同樂，數極自然變化，非是故相反駁。

translations.literal: The Five Emperors had differing rites, the Three Kings differing music—numbers exhaust and nature transforms—not deliberate contradiction.
translations.idiomatic: Five Emperors, three kings—each age reshapes ritual and music when patterns run their course.

sentences.zh: 德政不能救世混亂，賞罰豈足懲時清濁？

translations.literal: If virtuous government cannot rescue the world from confusion and disorder, how can rewards and punishments be enough to correct the age’s pure and impure?
translations.idiomatic: If good government cannot save a world in chaos, how can rewards and punishments sort the clean from the corrupt?

sentences.zh: 春秋時禍敗之始，戰國愈復增其荼毒。

translations.literal: Spring and Autumn began the trail of disaster; the Warring States doubled the poison.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn annals opened ruin; the Warring States poured on venom.

sentences.zh: 秦、汉无以相逾越，乃更加其怨酷。

translations.literal: Qin and Han could not surpass each other—they only added cruel spite.
translations.idiomatic: Qin and Han traded blows yet only stacked cruelty higher.

sentences.zh: 宁计生民之命，唯利己而自足。

translations.literal: They reckoned not the people's lives—sought only private ease.
translations.idiomatic: They weighed common lives at nothing and chased selfish gain.

sentences.zh: 於茲迄今，情僞萬方。

translations.literal: From this down to now, true and false take ten thousand forms.
translations.idiomatic: Since then, sham and sincerity have tangled in countless ways.

sentences.zh: 佞諂日熾，剛克消亡。

translations.literal: Flattery and sycophancy blaze day by day, while upright firmness disappears.
translations.idiomatic: Sycophants flare while backbone withers.

sentences.zh: 舐痔結駟，正色徒行。

translations.literal: Those who lick hemorrhoids hitch four-horse teams, while those of upright bearing walk on foot.
translations.idiomatic: Toadies ride matched teams while honest men walk.

sentences.zh: 嫗𡟥名勢，撫拍豪強。

translations.literal: The obsequious and fawning serve fame and power, stroking and patting the powerful.
translations.idiomatic: The fawning chase reputation and power, soothing and flattering the mighty.

sentences.zh: 偃蹇反俗，立致咎殃。

translations.literal: Proud withdrawal offends custom—disaster strikes at once.
translations.idiomatic: Stand aloof from fashion and ruin arrives overnight.

sentences.zh: 捷懾逐物，日富月昌。

translations.literal: Swift compliance chasing things grows richer day by day.
translations.idiomatic: Those who chase profit with nimble compliance wax wealthy monthly.

sentences.zh: 渾然同惑，孰温孰凉？

translations.literal: All muddled in the same delusion—who is warm and who is cold?
translations.idiomatic: The crowd shares one stupor—who still tells heat from chill?

sentences.zh: 邪夫顯進，直士幽藏。

translations.literal: Base men rise in sight; straight gentlemen hide in gloom.
translations.idiomatic: Villains vault into view while the upright vanish into shadow.

sentences.zh: 原斯瘼之攸興，實執政之匪賢。

translations.literal: Trace this plague's rise—the rulers truly lack worth.
translations.idiomatic: This sickness stems from unworthy men on the throne.

sentences.zh: 女谒掩其视听兮，近习秉其威权。

translations.literal: Women's pleas veil his ears and eyes; favorites grasp dread power.
translations.idiomatic: Female petitions blind him; attendants clutch terrible leverage.

sentences.zh: 所好則鑽皮出其毛羽，所惡則洗垢求其瘢痕。

translations.literal: Though one wishes to present sincerity and exhaust loyalty, the road is cut off and perilous, with no way forward.
translations.idiomatic: Even loyal words cannot cross that cliff; there is no path.

sentences.zh: 雖欲謁誠而盡忠，路絶嶮而靡緣。

translations.literal: Though one wishes to present sincerity and exhaust loyalty, the road is cut off and perilous, with no way forward.
translations.idiomatic: Even loyal words cannot cross that cliff; there is no path.

sentences.zh: 九重既不可启，又群吠之狺狺。

translations.literal: The ninefold gates will not open; packs of dogs yap between.
translations.idiomatic: Palace gates stay barred while kennel voices snarl.

sentences.zh: 安危于于旦夕，肆嗜欲于目前。

translations.literal: They toy with safety between dawn and dusk; indulge appetites before their eyes.
translations.idiomatic: They gamble the realm between meals and feed lust while it lasts.

sentences.zh: 奚異涉海之失舵，積薪而待燃？

translations.literal: How differs crossing sea without rudder—heaping fuel awaiting flame?
translations.idiomatic: That is sailing rudderless or stacking kindling for the spark.

sentences.zh: 榮納由於閃揄，孰知辯其蚩姸？

translations.literal: Advancement is received through fawning hints; who knows how to distinguish the ugly from the fair?
translations.idiomatic: Promotion rides on smirking praise; who can still tell beauty from ugliness?

sentences.zh: 故法禁屈撓干勢族，恩澤不逮於單門。

translations.literal: Thus laws and prohibitions bend and give way before powerful clans, while favor and grace do not reach solitary households.
translations.idiomatic: The law bends before great houses, while mercy never reaches poor doors.

sentences.zh: 寧飢寒於堯、舜之荒歲兮，不飽暖於當今之豐年。

translations.literal: Better to hunger and freeze in the lean years of Yao and Shun than to be full and warm in the abundant years of the present age.
translations.idiomatic: Better to starve in a sage-king’s famine than feast in the plenty of this age.

sentences.zh: 乘理雖死而非亡，違義雖生而匪存。

translations.literal: Ride principle though dead—not gone; betray justice though alive—not truly living.
translations.idiomatic: Stand on right—death cannot erase you; betray right—life is a walking corpse.

sentences.zh: 有秦客者，乃为诗曰：“河清不可俟，人命不可延。

translations.literal: A guest from Qin then versified: "The river cannot wait to clear; man's life cannot prolong."
translations.idiomatic: A western traveler sang that the Yellow River will not clear early and life cannot lengthen.

sentences.zh: 順風激靡草，富貴者稱賢。

translations.literal: A following wind lashes the bending grass; the rich and honored are called worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Wind bows the bending grass, and the wealthy pass for wise.

sentences.zh: 文籍雖滿腹，不如一囊錢。

translations.literal: Books filling the belly lose to one purse of cash.
translations.idiomatic: A packed library weighs less than one money sack.

sentences.zh: 伊優北堂上，抗臟倚門邊。

translations.literal: Buffoons are up in the northern hall, while the blunt and unbending lean beside the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Buffoons rule the high hall while the blunt-spoken wait by the door.

sentences.zh: 魯生聞此辭，繫而作歌曰：勢家多所宜，咳唾自成珠。

translations.literal: Lu Sheng hearing tied verse answered in song: powerful houses fit all things—spittle turns pearls.
translations.idiomatic: Master Lu took up the tune: grandees make every whim sacred—even spit becomes pearls.

sentences.zh: 被褐懷金玉，蘭蕙化爲芻。

translations.literal: Coarse sack hides gold and jade; orchids turn to fodder.
translations.idiomatic: Rough gowns conceal genius while orchids rot as hay.

sentences.zh: 贤者虽独悟，所困在群愚。

translations.literal: Worthies alone awake—trapped among blockheads.
translations.idiomatic: The wise see clearly yet suffocate among fools.

sentences.zh: 且各守爾分，勿復空馳驅。

translations.literal: Let each keep to his own allotment, and do not again gallop about in vain.
translations.idiomatic: Stay within your allotted place, and stop racing after emptiness.

sentences.zh: 哀哉復哀哉，此是命矣夫！

translations.literal: Let each keep to his own allotment, and do not again gallop about in vain.
translations.idiomatic: Stay within your allotted place, and stop racing after emptiness.

sentences.zh: 光和元年，舉郡上計，到京師。

translations.literal: Let each keep to his own allotment, and do not again gallop about in vain.
translations.idiomatic: Stay within your allotted place, and stop racing after emptiness.

sentences.zh: 是时，司徒袁逢受计，计吏数百人，皆拜伏庭中，莫敢仰视。

translations.literal: Minister Yuan Feng received accounts—hundreds of clerks all bowed in the courtyard—none dared look up.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Yuan Feng tallied registers while hundreds of clerks kowtowed and stared at the stones.

sentences.zh: 壹独长揖而已。

translations.literal: Yi alone performed a standing bow.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yi alone offered a long bow without kneeling.

sentences.zh: 逢望而异之，令左右往让之，曰：“下郡计吏而揖三公，何也？”

translations.literal: Feng saw him as strange—ordered attendants reproach—said a lower commandery clerk bows the Three Dukes—how?
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Feng stared, sent aides to scold him for bowing to three ministers instead of groveling.

sentences.zh: 对曰：“昔郦食其长揖汉王，今揖三公，何遽怪哉？”

translations.literal: He replied: "Anciently Li Yiji long bowed the King of Han—now I bow three ministers—why sudden wonder?"
translations.idiomatic: He answered that Li Yiji once bowed Emperor Gaozu upright—why fuss over three dukes?

sentences.zh: 逢则敛衽下堂，执其手，延置上坐，因问西方事，大悦，顾谓坐中曰：“此人汉阳赵元叔也。

translations.literal: Feng gathered his robes, descended the hall, took his hand, invited him to the upper seat—asked western affairs—and was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Feng straightened his robes, came down, clasped Zhao Yi's hand, seated him as chief guest, and questioned the northwest until delight overcame him.

sentences.zh: 朝臣莫有过之者，吾请为诸君分坐。”

translations.literal: Looking toward the assembly he said: "This man is Zhao Yuanshu of Hanyang—no courtier surpasses him—I ask to yield my seat to you all."
translations.idiomatic: Turning to the crowd he announced Zhao Yi of Hanyang outshone every minister and offered his own cushion.

sentences.zh: 坐者皆属观。

translations.literal: Those seated all craned to watch.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone twisted to stare.

sentences.zh: 既出，往造河南尹羊陟，不得见。

translations.literal: After leaving he visited Henan Governor Yang Zhi—not admitted.
translations.idiomatic: He called on Governor Yang Zhi of Henan and was turned away.

sentences.zh: 壹以公卿中非陟無足以託名者，乃日往到門，陟自強許通，尙臥未起。

translations.literal: Yi thought among dukes none but Zhi worth attaching his name—daily came to the gate—Zhi forced consent—still lay abed not risen.
translations.idiomatic: Believing only Yang Zhi worthy of patronage he returned daily until Yang agreed yet stayed in bed.

sentences.zh: 壹徑入上堂，遂前臨之，曰：「竊伏西州，承高風舊矣。

translations.literal: Yi strode straight into the hall—approached the couch—said "I lay hidden in the western provinces long admiring your lofty manner."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yi marched to the bedside praising Yang's fame from afar.

sentences.zh: 乃今方遇而忽然，奈何命也！”

translations.literal: "Now we meet yet like sudden death—alas fate!"
translations.idiomatic: Meeting you now feels like facing mortality—such is fate.

sentences.zh: 因举声哭，门下惊，皆奔入满侧。

translations.literal: He raised his voice and wept—the gate guards panic—all rushed in filling the sides.
translations.idiomatic: He wailed aloud until servants poured in.

sentences.zh: 陟知其非常人，乃起，延与语，大奇之。

translations.literal: Zhi knew he was no ordinary man—rose—extended talk—greatly admired him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhi realized genius, rose, and talked until admiration overcame him.

sentences.zh: 谓曰：“子出矣。”

translations.literal: said "you may go"
translations.idiomatic: He told him to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 陟明旦大从车骑，奉谒造壹。

translations.literal: Next dawn Zhi with great train of carriages visited Yi.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Yang arrived with a grand cavalcade to call on Zhao Yi.

sentences.zh: 时，诸计吏多盛饬车马帷幕，而壹独柴车草屏，露宿其傍，延陟前坐于车下，左右莫不叹愕。

translations.literal: Other clerks used ornate carriages and curtains—Yi alone used firewood cart and straw screen—lodged in the open beside—invited Zhi to sit beneath the cart—attendants gasped.
translations.idiomatic: Peer clerks paraded silk drapes while Zhao slept under a reed screen beside a lumber wagon and seated Yang under the axle—stunning onlookers.

sentences.zh: 陟遂与言谈，至熏夕，极欢而去，执其手曰：“良璞不剖，必有泣血以相明者矣！”

translations.literal: Zhi talked till dusk smoke—utmost joy departed—held his hand said fine jade uncut must have blood tears to prove.
translations.idiomatic: They talked till evening smoke curled; Yang gripped his hand likening him to uncut jade worth bleeding for.

sentences.zh: 陟乃与袁逢共称荐之。

translations.literal: Zhi with Yuan Feng jointly recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhi and Yuan Feng recommended him together.

sentences.zh: 名动京师，士大夫想望其风采。

translations.literal: His name shook the capital—gentlemen imagined his bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang buzzed with his name; scholars dreamed of meeting him.

sentences.zh: 及西还，道经弘农，过侯太守皇甫规，门者不即通，壹遂遁去。

translations.literal: Returning west he passed Hongnong—visited Prefect Huangfu Gui—the gate delayed entry—Yi fled.
translations.idiomatic: Heading home through Hongnong he called on Huangfu Gui; slow admission made him slip away.

sentences.zh: 门吏惧，以白之，规闻壹名大惊，乃追书谢曰：“蹉跌不面，企德怀风，虚心委质，为日久矣。

translations.literal: Gate guards feared and reported—Gui heard Yi's name greatly alarmed—sent letter apologizing "I stumbled and missed meeting—long admired your wind—submitted heart many days."
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Gui panicked and mailed an apology for missing the visit.

sentences.zh: 侧闻仁者愍其区区，冀承清诲，以释遥悚。

translations.literal: "Heard sideways humane pity my petty self—hoped clear teaching would ease distant fear."
translations.idiomatic: He begged instruction to calm old fears.

sentences.zh: 今旦，外白有一尉两计吏，不道屈尊门下，更启乃知已去。

translations.literal: "This morning outside reported one captain two clerks unknown honored gate—reopened learned already gone."
translations.idiomatic: Morning clerks spoke of the visitors too late—by reopening the gate Zhao had gone.

sentences.zh: 如印绶可投，夜岂待旦。

translations.literal: "If seal could cast aside night would not wait dawn."
translations.idiomatic: Had he known he would have renounced office overnight.

sentences.zh: 惟君明睿，平其夙心。

translations.literal: "Only you wise—level early intent."
translations.idiomatic: Only your clarity can steady what we felt before.

sentences.zh: 寧當慢慠，加於所天。

translations.literal: "Would I slight arrogance toward heaven-master?"
translations.idiomatic: Would I dare insult my sovereign patron?

sentences.zh: 事在悖惑，不足具責。

translations.literal: "Matter confused—not worth full blame."
translations.idiomatic: Confusion explains it—no need for harsh blame.

sentences.zh: 倘可原察，追修前好，则何福如之！

translations.literal: "If you can forgive and investigate—restore former goodwill—what blessing could compare!"
translations.idiomatic: If you forgive and renew friendship—what fortune tops that?

sentences.zh: 謹遣主簿奉書。

translations.literal: I respectfully dispatch my chief clerk to present this letter.
translations.idiomatic: I have sent my chief clerk to deliver this letter with my respects.

sentences.zh: 下筆氣結，汗流竟趾。」

translations.literal: Setting brush to silk knots my breath; sweat streams even to my toes.
translations.idiomatic: My hand shakes as I write—sweat runs to my feet.

sentences.zh: 壹報曰：「君學成師範，縉紳歸慕，仰高希驥，歷年滋多。

translations.literal: Yi replied: "Your learning has become a model for teachers, and officials turn to you in admiration; for many years I have looked up to your height and hoped to follow the thoroughbred."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yi replied, "Your learning sets a standard for teachers, and officials admire you; for years I have looked up to you and hoped to follow in your tracks."

sentences.zh: 旋轅兼道，渴於言侍，沐浴晨興，昧旦守門，實望仁君，昭其懸遲。

translations.literal: You raced chariot double tracks—burned to attend my words—bathed at dawn—waited before dawn at my gate—truly hoped a humane lord would ease long suspense.
translations.idiomatic: You hurried back along both roads, longing for conversation, rose bathed before light, and waited at his gate hoping kindness would end the strain.

sentences.zh: 以貴下賤，握發垂接。

translations.literal: Though exalted you humbled yourself toward the low—like the Duke of Zhou grasped dripping hair mid-bath.
translations.idiomatic: You stooped from high rank to meet a nobody—the courtesy of a ruler who interrupts his shampoo.

sentences.zh: 高可敷玩墳典，起發聖意；

translations.literal: On high you might unfold tomb classics and awaken sage intent.
translations.idiomatic: At best you could unpack canonical texts and stir sagely purpose.

sentences.zh: 下則抗論當世，消弭時災。

translations.literal: Below you might debate the age and dissolve present calamity.
translations.idiomatic: At least you could argue policy and lift today's disasters.

sentences.zh: 豈悟君子，自生怠倦，失恂恂善誘之德，同亡國驕惰之志！

translations.literal: Who could guess the noble master grew weary himself—lost humbly coaxing virtue—shared the ruined state's arrogant laziness!
translations.idiomatic: Instead you slid into sloth like a doomed dynasty—where was the gentle persuasion?

sentences.zh: 蓋見機而作，不俟終日，是以夙退自引，畏使君勞。

translations.literal: Seeing the moment I withdrew—not waiting the whole day—therefore withdrew early myself—feared tiring my lord.
translations.idiomatic: So I left before the day was out rather than burden you further.

sentences.zh: 昔人或歷説而不遇，或思士而無從，皆歸之於天，不尤於物。

translations.literal: Anciently some toured persuading yet never met opportunity—some sought scholars yet found none—all blamed Heaven—not blamed circumstance.
translations.idiomatic: Old tales blame Heaven when persuasion fails—not the world itself.

sentences.zh: 今壹自譴而已，豈敢有猜！

translations.literal: Now Yi blames only himself—how dare harbor suspicion!
translations.idiomatic: I fault only myself—no shadow of doubt toward you.

sentences.zh: 仁君忽一匹夫，於德何損？

translations.literal: If a noble lord overlooks one commoner—what harm to virtue?
translations.idiomatic: Ignoring one nobody cannot stain your virtue.

sentences.zh: 而遠辱手筆，追路相尋，誠足愧也。

translations.literal: Yet you humble yourself with personal brush chasing down the road—truly enough to shame me.
translations.idiomatic: Yet your letter chasing me down the road humbles me past bearing.

sentences.zh: 壹之區區，曷云量己？

translations.literal: Yi's petty self—how speak of measuring himself?
translations.idiomatic: How should a nobody like me weigh his own worth?

sentences.zh: 其嗟可去，謝也可食，誠則頑薄，實識其趣。

translations.literal: If the contemptuous call can be put aside, and food offered with apology can be eaten, then though I am stubborn and shallow, I truly understand the point.
translations.idiomatic: Once the insult is removed, even the offered meal can be accepted; coarse as I am, I understand your meaning.

sentences.zh: 但關節疢動，膝炙壞潰，請俟他日，乃奉其情。

translations.literal: But my joints are painfully stirred and the moxa burns on my knees have broken open; please wait for another day, and then I will offer my true feelings.
translations.idiomatic: My joints are aching and the cautery wounds on my knees have opened; give me another day, and I will speak my mind fully.

sentences.zh: 輒誦來貺，永以自慰。」

translations.literal: I repeatedly recite your gracious gift and forever use it to comfort myself.
translations.idiomatic: I keep rereading your generous words and take lasting comfort from them.

sentences.zh: 遂去不顾。

translations.literal: Thereupon left without turning back.
translations.idiomatic: He walked away and never looked back.

sentences.zh: 州郡争致礼命，十辟公府，并不就，终于家。

translations.literal: Provinces vied to extend ritual summons—ten calls from Excellencies' offices—accepted none—ended life at home.
translations.idiomatic: Every province courted him; ten grand offices summoned him—he refused all and died at home.

sentences.zh: 初袁逢使善相者相壹，云“仕不过郡吏”，竟如其言。

translations.literal: First Yuan Feng had a physiognomist read Yi—said rank would not pass commandery clerk—finally matched prediction.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Feng once had his face read: ‘No higher than commandery clerk’—it came true.

sentences.zh: 著賦、頌、箴、誄、書、論及雜文十六篇。

translations.literal: He composed fu, hymns, admonitions, dirges, letters, treatises, and miscellaneous pieces—sixteen works.
translations.idiomatic: Sixteen pieces survive: fu, songs, warnings, laments, essays, and scraps.

sentences.zh: 刘梁字曼山，一名岑，东平宁阳人也。

translations.literal: Liu Liang courtesy Manshan—also called Cen—was a native of Ningyang in Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Liang, styled Manshan—also known as Cen—hailed from Ningyang in Dongping.

sentences.zh: 梁宗室子孫，而少孤貧，賣書於市以自資。

translations.literal: He was imperial descendant yet orphaned poor—sold books in market to support himself.
translations.idiomatic: Of royal blood but fatherless and poor, he peddled books for rice.

sentences.zh: 常疾世多利交，以邪曲相党，乃著《破群论》。

translations.literal: He often hated the age's profit-seeking alliances—crooked factions banding—thereupon composed 《Breaking Cliques》.
translations.idiomatic: He despised mercenary cliques and wrote 《Breaking Cliques》.

sentences.zh: 时之览者以为：“仲尼作《春秋》，乱臣知惧。

translations.literal: Readers at the time said: "Confucius composed Spring and Autumn—disloyal ministers feared."
translations.idiomatic: They compared him to Confucius: the Spring and Autumn froze traitors in fear.

sentences.zh: 今此论之作，俗士岂不愧心！”

translations.literal: Now this essay's creation—would vulgar scholars not blush at heart!
translations.idiomatic: They asked how corrupt scholars could read it without shame.

sentences.zh: 其文不存。

translations.literal: Its text does not survive.
translations.idiomatic: That work is lost.

sentences.zh: 又著《辩和同之论》。

translations.literal: He also composed 《Discourse on Harmonizing Same and Different》.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote 《Discourse on Harmonizing Same and Different》.

sentences.zh: 其辞曰：

translations.literal: Its words say:
translations.idiomatic: It begins:

sentences.zh: 夫事有违而得道，有顺而失义，有爱而为害，有恶而为美。

translations.literal: Affairs exist opposing yet gaining the Way—compliant yet losing right—love turning harmful—hate turning beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: Some roads look wrong yet lead right; some smooth paths betray justice; affection harms; hatred heals.

sentences.zh: 其故何乎？

translations.literal: What is the reason?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 盖明智之所得，暗伪之所失也。

translations.literal: What the wise attain—the dull and false lose.
translations.idiomatic: Insight wins what folly forfeits.

sentences.zh: 是以君子之于事也，无适无莫，必考之以义焉。

translations.literal: Therefore toward affairs the gentleman neither rigidly approves nor rejects—must examine by righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: The nobleman weighs each case by righteousness, not reflex.

sentences.zh: 得由和兴，失由同起，故以可济否谓之和，好恶不殊谓之同。

translations.literal: Gain arises from harmony—loss arises from uniformity—therefore aiding imbalance is called harmony—sharing identical likes is called uniformity.
translations.idiomatic: Harmony mixes unlike tones to save disorder; uniformity means everyone liking the same.

sentences.zh: 《春秋传》曰：“和如羹焉，酸苦以剂其味，君子食之以平其心。

translations.literal: Spring Autumn Commentary says harmony is like stew—sour and bitter balance flavor—the gentleman eats it to steady mind.
translations.idiomatic: The Zuo tradition compares harmony to seasoned stew—bitter and sour balance the palate.

sentences.zh: 同如水焉，若以水济水，谁能食之？

translations.literal: Uniformity is like water—if water dilutes water—who can drink?
translations.idiomatic: Uniformity is water added to water—no one can swallow it.

sentences.zh: 琴瑟之专一，谁能听之？”

translations.literal: Zither and se fixed on one note—who can listen?
translations.idiomatic: If every string plays one note, no ear stays tuned.

sentences.zh: 是以君子之行，周而不比，和而不同；

translations.literal: Hence gentleman's conduct circles wide yet does not faction—harmonizes yet not uniform.
translations.idiomatic: So the gentleman encompasses many voices without cliques—harmony without conformity.

sentences.zh: 以救过为正，以匡恶为忠。

translations.literal: Correcting faults counts as upright—rebuking evil counts as loyal.
translations.idiomatic: Naming fault is honesty; naming evil is loyalty.

sentences.zh: 經曰：「將順其美，匡救其惡，則上下和睦能相親也。」

translations.literal: If, through the spirits of the ancestral temple, I can keep my head until death, please make me Ling or Li.
translations.idiomatic: If the ancestral spirits let me die with my head intact, give me the posthumous name Ling or Li."

translations.idiomatic: If the ancestral spirits let me die with my head intact, give me the posthumous name Ling or Li."

translations.literal: If, through the spirits of the ancestral temple, I can keep my head until death, please make me Ling or Li.
translations.idiomatic: If the ancestral spirits let me die with my head intact, give me the posthumous name Ling or Li."

translations.literal: If, through the spirits of the ancestral temple, I can keep my head until death, please make me Ling or Li.
translations.idiomatic: If the ancestral spirits let me die with my head intact, give me the posthumous name Ling or Li."

translations.idiomatic: If the ancestral spirits let me die with my head intact, give me the posthumous name Ling or Li."

sentences.zh: 及其卒也，子囊曰：“不然。

translations.literal: At death Zinang said not so.
translations.idiomatic: At his death Minister Zinang disagreed.

sentences.zh: 夫事君者，從其善，不從其過。

translations.literal: Serving lord—follow his good—not his faults.
translations.idiomatic: Serve the ruler's virtue, not his vices.

sentences.zh: 赫赫楚國，而君臨之，撫正南海，訓及諸夏，其寵大矣。

translations.literal: Majestic Chu—and lord faces it—pacifies southern seas—instructs Hua lands—favor vast.
translations.idiomatic: Chu blazes bright under him—he faces the southern seas and teaches the Central States—honor immense.

sentences.zh: 有是寵也，而知其過，可不謂恭乎！」

translations.literal: Having such favor yet knowing fault—can we not call reverent!
translations.idiomatic: Knowing one's fault despite such glory—is that not true reverence?

sentences.zh: 大夫众之。

translations.literal: Ministers praised him.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers acclaimed him.

sentences.zh: 此諱而得道者也。

translations.literal: This is being compliant while losing righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: That is obedience at the cost of righteousness.

sentences.zh: 及靈王驕淫，暴虐無度，芋尹申亥從王之欲，以殯於乾溪，殉之二女。

translations.literal: This is being compliant while losing righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: That is obedience at the cost of righteousness.

sentences.zh: 此順而失義者也。

translations.literal: This is being compliant while losing righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: That is obedience at the cost of righteousness.

sentences.zh: 鄢陵之役，晉楚對戰，陽穀獻酒，子反以斃。

translations.literal: This is being compliant while losing righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: That is obedience at the cost of righteousness.

sentences.zh: 此爱而害之者也。

translations.literal: This is love harming.
translations.idiomatic: Love that destroys.

sentences.zh: 臧武仲曰：“孟孙之恶我，药石也；

translations.literal: Zang Wu Zhong said: "Mengsun's hatred of me is medicine and whetstone;"
translations.idiomatic: Zang Wu Zhong said: "Mengsun's spite is the bitter cure I need;"

sentences.zh: 季孙之爱我，美疢也。

translations.literal: Jisun's love for me is a fair tumor.
translations.idiomatic: and Jisun's fondness is a glossy ulcer.

sentences.zh: 疢毒滋厚，石犹生我。”

translations.literal: Though the tumor's poison grows thick, the stone still gives me life."
translations.idiomatic: Even as the growth festers, the harsh stone keeps me alive.

sentences.zh: 此恶而为美者也。

translations.literal: This is how hatred becomes a kind of grace.
translations.idiomatic: That is how a curse can wear beauty's mask.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：「智之難也！

translations.literal: Confucius said: "How hard it is to be wise!
translations.idiomatic: Confucius cried: "True wisdom is rare!"

sentences.zh: 有臧武仲之智，而不容於魯國，抑有由也。

translations.literal: Though one had Zang Wu Zhong's wit—he still found no room in Lu—indeed there was cause.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Wu Zhong's brilliance could not win Lu—and not without reason.

sentences.zh: 作不順而施不恕也。」

translations.literal: His conduct ran counter to the Way and his mercy never reached others."
translations.idiomatic: He acted against principle and showed no humane breadth.

sentences.zh: 蓋善其知義，譏其違道也。

translations.literal: This praised his knowing what was right and criticized his departing from the Way.
translations.idiomatic: The comment praises his sense of duty but faults him for leaving the Way.

sentences.zh: 夫知而違之，僞也；

translations.literal: To know it and yet go against it is falseness;
translations.idiomatic: Knowing what is right and doing otherwise is hypocrisy;

sentences.zh: 不知而失之，暗也。

translations.literal: Not to know and therefore to fail is darkness.
translations.idiomatic: Ignorance that misses the mark is blindness.

sentences.zh: 暗爲僞焉，其患一也。

translations.literal: Darkness and hypocrisy share one wound.
translations.idiomatic: Blindness and deceit injure alike.

sentences.zh: 患之所在，非徒在智之不及，又在及而違這者矣。

translations.literal: The harm lies not only in wisdom falling short—but also in possessing wisdom yet turning against it.
translations.idiomatic: Calamity comes from stupidity and from intellect betrayed.

sentences.zh: 故曰“智及之，仁不能守之，虽得之，必失之”也。

translations.literal: Hence it is said: "Though wisdom reach there, if benevolence cannot guard it, though you gain it you will surely lose it."
translations.idiomatic: So the Analects: wisdom without humanity cannot hold what it seizes.

sentences.zh: 《夏書》曰：「念茲在茲，庶事恕施。」

translations.literal: The Xia Documents says: "Hold this ever in mind—in all affairs apply humane forgiveness."
translations.idiomatic: The canon bids us remember and meet every duty with charity.

sentences.zh: 忠智之謂矣。

translations.literal: That is what loyal wisdom means."
translations.idiomatic: That is faithful insight.

sentences.zh: 故君子之行，動則思義，不爲利回，不爲義疚，進退周旋，唯道是務。

translations.literal: Hence the gentleman's conduct—when he moves he weighs righteousness—not swayed by profit—not shamed from duty—advancing and retreating he wheels only on the Way.
translations.idiomatic: So the nobleman acts from principle—never bought by gain or cowed from right.

sentences.zh: 苟失其道，则兄弟不阿；

translations.literal: If he loses the Way—even brothers withhold partiality.
translations.idiomatic: Lose the Way and kin will not bend the rule for you.

sentences.zh: 苟得其義，雖仇讎不廢。

translations.literal: If one obtains what is right, even an enemy is not discarded.
translations.idiomatic: When right conduct is present, even an enemy should not be cast aside.

translations.idiomatic: When right conduct is present, even an enemy should not be cast aside.

sentences.zh: 不在憎爱，以道为贵。”

translations.literal: "not in hating or loving but in treasuring the Way."
translations.idiomatic: Not love or hate but holding fast to the Way.

sentences.zh: 《礼记》曰：“爱而知其恶，憎而知其善。”

translations.literal: The Book of Rites says: 'Though you love him, know his faults; though you hate him, know his virtues.'"
translations.idiomatic: The Rites demand we see flaw in the beloved and merit in the hated.

sentences.zh: 考义之谓也。

translations.literal: This is what is called weighing righteousness."
translations.idiomatic: That is judging by moral weight.

sentences.zh: 延目廣望，聘觀終日。

translations.literal: Ahead lay the waters of the Huai; to the left, the waves of Dongting; to the right he looked toward the recesses of Pengli; to the south he gazed at the slopes of Wushan.
translations.idiomatic: Before him ran the Huai; Dongting surged to the left, Pengli’s inlets opened to the right, and Wushan rose to the south.

sentences.zh: 顧謂左史倚相曰：「盛哉斯樂，可以遺老而忘死也！」

translations.literal: Ahead lay the waters of the Huai; to the left, the waves of Dongting; to the right he looked toward the recesses of Pengli; to the south he gazed at the slopes of Wushan.
translations.idiomatic: Before him ran the Huai; Dongting surged to the left, Pengli’s inlets opened to the right, and Wushan rose to the south.

sentences.zh: 於是遂作章華之臺，築乾谿之室，窮木土之技，單珍府之實。

translations.literal: Ahead lay the waters of the Huai; to the left, the waves of Dongting; to the right he looked toward the recesses of Pengli; to the south he gazed at the slopes of Wushan.
translations.idiomatic: Before him ran the Huai; Dongting surged to the left, Pengli’s inlets opened to the right, and Wushan rose to the south.

sentences.zh: 举国营之，数年乃成。

translations.literal: The whole state labored—several years before it was finished.
translations.idiomatic: The whole kingdom toiled for years before it stood complete.

sentences.zh: 設長夜之淫宴，作北裏之新聲。

translations.literal: He then composed this fu to admonish him: descended from Gaoyang's line, you inherit the vast bounty of your sagely ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: So he wrote this rhapsody to warn him: born of Gaoyang's line, you inherited your sacred ancestor's great grace.

sentences.zh: 於是伍舉知夫陳、蔡之將生謀也。

translations.literal: He then composed this fu to admonish him: descended from Gaoyang's line, you inherit the vast bounty of your sagely ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: So he wrote this rhapsody to warn him: born of Gaoyang's line, you inherited your sacred ancestor's great grace.

sentences.zh: 乃作斯賦以諷之：胄高陽之苗胤兮，承聖祖之洪澤。

translations.literal: He then composed this fu to admonish him: descended from Gaoyang's line, you inherit the vast bounty of your sagely ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: So he wrote this rhapsody to warn him: born of Gaoyang's line, you inherited your sacred ancestor's great grace.

sentences.zh: 建列籓于南楚兮，等威灵于二伯。

translations.literal: Raised feudal screens in southern Chu—matched awesome spirit with the Two Earls.
translations.idiomatic: He planted kings across southern Chu and rivaled the Two Regents in dread majesty.

sentences.zh: 超有商之大彭兮，越隆周之兩虢。

translations.literal: Surpassed Shang's mighty Peng—crossed flourishing Zhou's twin Guo.
translations.idiomatic: He outdid Great Peng of Shang and the paired Guo lords of high Zhou.

sentences.zh: 達皇佐之高勛兮，馳仁聲之顯赫。

translations.literal: He reached the high merit of imperial assistants and sent the brilliance of his humane reputation racing abroad.
translations.idiomatic: He matched the great achievements of royal counselors, and his bright name for benevolence sped through the realm.

sentences.zh: 惠風春施，神武電斷，華夏肅清，五服攸亂。

translations.literal: His gracious wind spread like spring; his divine martial power decided like lightning; Huaxia was solemnly cleared, and the Five Dependencies were thereby ordered.
translations.idiomatic: Grace moved like spring wind and force struck like lightning; the heartland was cleared, and every tribute zone fell into order.

sentences.zh: 旦垂精於萬機兮，夕回輦於門館。

translations.literal: At dawn he bent his full attention to the myriad affairs; at dusk he turned his carriage back to the gates and lodges.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he gave himself to the affairs of state; by dusk his carriage turned back to the palace lodges.

sentences.zh: 設長夜之歡飲兮，展中情之嬿婉。

translations.literal: He set out long-night revels and unfolded the gentle grace of his inner feelings.
translations.idiomatic: He staged all-night banquets, letting his private affection unfold in tender ease.

sentences.zh: 竭四海之妙珍兮，尽生人之秘玩。

translations.literal: He drained the four seas of wonders—spent every mortal luxury.
translations.idiomatic: He exhausted the empire's treasures and every secret delight of the living.

sentences.zh: 爾乃攜窈窕，從好仇，徑肉林，登糟丘，蘭肴山竦，椒酒淵流。

translations.literal: Then he led slim beauties and chosen mates—cut through forests of meat—climbed hills of dregs—orchid dishes piled like peaks—pepper wine poured like an abyss.
translations.idiomatic: Then came slender girls and worthy companions, paths through flesh and lees, orchid viands mountain-high and peppered wine deep as a gorge.

sentences.zh: 激玄醴于清池兮，靡微风而行舟。

translations.literal: He whipped dark must in clear pools—followed faint breeze to row boats.
translations.idiomatic: They beat sweet wine in glass pools and drifted boats on the lightest wind.

sentences.zh: 登瑤臺以回望兮，冀彌日而消憂。

translations.literal: He mounted the jade terrace to look about—hoped a whole day would melt care.
translations.idiomatic: From the jade terrace they gazed wide, wishing daylight could wash sorrow away.

sentences.zh: 於是招宓妃，命湘娥，齊倡列，鄭女羅。

translations.literal: Thereupon he summoned Fu Fei—commanded the ladies of the Xiang—lined Qi singers—spread Zheng girls in rows.
translations.idiomatic: They called Fu Fei and the Xiang maidens, ranked Qi choruses and Zheng dancers in silken files.

sentences.zh: 揚《激楚》之清宮兮，展新聲而長歌。

translations.literal: He raised the clear strains of "Ji Chu"—unfolded new songs in long pulls.
translations.idiomatic: They lifted the clear notes of "Ji Chu" and spun fresh melodies in drawn-out song.

sentences.zh: 繁手超於北裏，妙舞麗於《陽阿》。

translations.literal: Busy fingers outdid Beili—wonderful dances rivaled "Yang E".
translations.idiomatic: Fingerwork surpassed Beili's tricks; the dance matched "Yang E" in grace.

sentences.zh: 金石類聚，絲竹群分。

translations.literal: Bronze and stone massed together—silk and bamboo answered in parts.
translations.idiomatic: Metal and stone chimed in chorus; strings and winds traded phrases.

sentences.zh: 神輕袿，曳華文，羅衣飄颻，組綺繽紛。

translations.literal: Spirit-like in light gowns, trailing splendid patterns; gauze robes fluttered, and patterned sashes scattered in profusion.
translations.idiomatic: In airy gowns and trailing brocade, gauze fluttered and bright sashes flashed.

sentences.zh: 縱輕軀以迅赴，若孤鵠之失群；

translations.literal: They released their light bodies in swift motion, like a lone swan separated from its flock;
translations.idiomatic: Light bodies darted forward like a lone swan cut off from the flock;

sentences.zh: 振華袂以逶迤，若遊龍之登雲。

translations.literal: He flourished patterned sleeves in long waves—as a roaming dragon climbs the clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Sleeves opened in long curves like dragons mounting mist.

sentences.zh: 於是歡嬿旣洽，長夜向半，琴瑟易調，繁手改彈。

translations.literal: Thereupon joy and beauty had mingled—long night neared half—lutes changed tuning—busy fingers switched their plucking.
translations.idiomatic: Delight had peaked toward midnight; they retuned zithers and changed to new finger-songs.

sentences.zh: 清聲發而響激，微音逝而流散。

translations.literal: Clear tones burst sharp—faint notes faded and scattered on the air.
translations.idiomatic: Bright notes cracked like ice; soft phrases melted away.

sentences.zh: 振弱支而紆繞兮，若綠繁之垂干；

translations.literal: Slender limbs twisted and looped—as green abundance hangs from the bough;
translations.idiomatic: Slender arms coiled like vine heavy on a branch.

sentences.zh: 忽飄颻以輕逝兮，似鸞飛於天漢。

translations.literal: Suddenly they drifted lightly away, like a luan flying in the Milky Way.
translations.idiomatic: Then they lifted away as lightly as a luan in the River of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 舞無常態，鼓無定節，尋聲響應，修短靡跌。

translations.literal: The dance had no fixed form and the drums no fixed beat; following the sounds, they answered in resonance, and long and short measures never stumbled.
translations.idiomatic: Dance and drum refused fixed patterns; every phrase was answered, long or short, without a missed step.

sentences.zh: 長袖奮而生風，清氣激而繞結。

translations.literal: Long sleeves lashed and raised wind—clear breath struck and knotted round.
translations.idiomatic: Long sleeves whipped a gale; pure tone twisted and held.

sentences.zh: 爾乃姸媚遞進，巧弄相加，俯仰異容，忽兮神化。

translations.literal: Then loveliness advanced in layers—clever tricks piled—bow and rise shifted every face—suddenly spirit-like transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Grace stacked trick on trick; each gesture turned a new mask—then sudden as gods changing form.

sentences.zh: 體迅輕鴻，榮曜春華，進如浮雲，退如激波。

translations.literal: Their bodies were swift as light wild geese, radiant as spring blossoms; they advanced like floating clouds and retreated like surging waves.
translations.idiomatic: Bodies flashed like light geese and spring flowers, advancing like clouds and drawing back like breaking waves.

sentences.zh: 雖復柳惠，能不咨嗟！

translations.literal: Even Liu Xiaohui—could he hold back a sigh!
translations.idiomatic: Even Liu Xiaohui could not choke down a sigh!

sentences.zh: 於是天河旣回，淫樂未終，清籥發徵，《激楚》揚風。

translations.literal: Thereupon the night's river had wheeled—debauch not yet ended—clear flute sounded the zhi mode—"Ji Chu" rode the gale.
translations.idiomatic: The sky turned on; revel continued—the reed piped zhi and "Ji Chu" rode the wind.

sentences.zh: 於是音氣發於絲竹兮，飛響軼於雲中。

translations.literal: Thereupon tone-breath rose from strings and pipes—flying echoes passed beyond the clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Sound welled from silk and bamboo and flew past the clouds.

sentences.zh: 比目應節而雙躍兮，孤雌感聲而鳴雄。

translations.literal: The paired flatfish leapt together to the beat, and the lone female, moved by the sound, called to the male.
translations.idiomatic: Paired fish jumped in time, and a lone female bird, stirred by the music, called for her mate.

sentences.zh: 美繁手之輕妙兮，嘉新聲之彌隆。

translations.literal: They praised the light busy fingers—praised the new sound's mounting swell.
translations.idiomatic: They marveled at nimble hands and the rising new refrains.

sentences.zh: 于是众变已尽，群乐既考。

translations.literal: Thereupon every change had run—all music had ended.
translations.idiomatic: Every variation was spent; the suite had played through.

sentences.zh: 歸乎生風之廣夏兮，修黃軒之要道。

translations.literal: They returned to the wind-swept vast hall—cultivated the Yellow August's vital way.
translations.idiomatic: They withdrew to the breezy hall and took up the Yellow Emperor's high road.

sentences.zh: 攜西子之弱腕兮，援毛嬪之素肘。

translations.literal: He took Xizi's slender wrists—supported Mao Concubine's pale arms.
translations.idiomatic: He clasped West Beauty's wrists and Mao Concubine's moon-white elbows.

sentences.zh: 形便娟以嬋媛兮，若流風之靡草。

translations.literal: Forms graceful and lovely—as wind bends the grass.
translations.idiomatic: Grace brushed him like wind combing grass.

sentences.zh: 美儀操之姣麗兮，忽遺生而忘老。

translations.literal: He praised deportment's splendor—forgot living and forgot age.
translations.idiomatic: Such beauty made him forget life itself and forget growing old.

sentences.zh: 爾乃清夜晨，妙技單，收尊俎，徹鼓盤。

translations.literal: Then night thinned toward dawn—wonders ended—gathered cups and stands—withdrew drums and trays.
translations.idiomatic: As dawn neared they struck the show, cleared goblets and platters, pulled away the drums.

sentences.zh: 惘焉若酲，撫劍而嘆。

translations.literal: Dazed as if sobering from wine, he stroked his sword and sighed.
translations.idiomatic: He came to himself as if after wine, touched his sword, and sighed.

sentences.zh: 慮理國之須才，悟稼穡之艱難。

translations.literal: He considered that ordering the state required talent, and understood the hardships of sowing and reaping.
translations.idiomatic: He remembered that government needs able men and that farming is hard labor.

sentences.zh: 美呂尙之佐周，善管仲之輔桓。

translations.literal: He praised Lü Shang's aid to Zhou—praised Guan Zhong's service to Huan.
translations.idiomatic: He praised Lü Wang for Zhou and Guan Zhong for Duke Huan.

sentences.zh: 將超世而作理，焉沈湎於此歡！

translations.literal: He would transcend the age and set order right—how could he drown in these pleasures!
translations.idiomatic: He meant to lift the realm with good rule—how wallow in delight!

sentences.zh: 於是罷女樂，墮瑤臺。

translations.literal: Thereupon he dismissed the female musicians and demolished the jade terrace.
translations.idiomatic: So he sent the dancers away and tore down the jade terrace.

sentences.zh: 思夏禹之卑官，慕有虞之土階。

translations.literal: He pondered Xia Yu's humble palace—admired You Shun's earthen steps.
translations.idiomatic: He remembered Yu's low halls and Shun's packed-earth stairs.

sentences.zh: 舉英奇於仄陋，拔髦秀於蓬萊。

translations.literal: He raised heroes from mean lanes—plucked excellence from Penglai.
translations.idiomatic: He drew genius from the gutter and culled worth from Penglai's isles.

sentences.zh: 君明哲以知人，官隨任而處能。

translations.literal: The ruler saw clearly to know men—offices matched duty and seated ability.
translations.idiomatic: The lord read men truly and set each post where talent fit.

sentences.zh: 百揆時敍，庶績咸熙。

translations.literal: The hundred ministries fell in order—every task shone.
translations.idiomatic: All government aligned; every deed succeeded.

sentences.zh: 诸侯慕义，不召同期。

translations.literal: Feudal lords admired righteousness—without summons they came together.
translations.idiomatic: Lords rallied to duty without waiting to be called.

sentences.zh: 繼高陽之絶軌，崇成、莊之洪基。

translations.literal: He continued Gaoyang's peerless course and exalted the vast foundation of Cheng and Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Gaoyang's unmatched path and raised high the foundation laid by Cheng and Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 雖齊醒之一匡，豈足方於大持？

translations.literal: He continued Gaoyang's peerless course and exalted the vast foundation of Cheng and Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Gaoyang's unmatched path and raised high the foundation laid by Cheng and Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 尔乃育之以仁，临之以明。

translations.literal: Then he nurtured them with humaneness—oversaw them with clarity.
translations.idiomatic: Then he reared the people in kindness and ruled them with clear sight.

sentences.zh: 致虔報於鬼神，盡肅恭乎上京。

translations.literal: When he arrived, He Jin appointed him as a clerk and received him with ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: When Bian Rang arrived, He Jin named him clerk and received him with full courtesy.

sentences.zh: 馳淳化於黎元，永歷世而太平。

translations.literal: When he arrived, He Jin appointed him as a clerk and received him with ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: When Bian Rang arrived, He Jin named him clerk and received him with full courtesy.

sentences.zh: 大將軍何進聞讓才名，欲辟命之。

translations.literal: When he arrived, He Jin appointed him as a clerk and received him with ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: When Bian Rang arrived, He Jin named him clerk and received him with full courtesy.

sentences.zh: 恐不至，詭以軍事徵召。

translations.literal: When he arrived, He Jin appointed him as a clerk and received him with ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: When Bian Rang arrived, He Jin named him clerk and received him with full courtesy.

sentences.zh: 旣到，署令史，進以禮見之。

translations.literal: When he arrived, He Jin appointed him as a clerk and received him with ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: When Bian Rang arrived, He Jin named him clerk and received him with full courtesy.

sentences.zh: 让善占射，能辞对。

translations.literal: Rang excelled at riddle-contests and repartee.
translations.idiomatic: Rang shone at guessing games and quick answers.

sentences.zh: 时，宾客满堂，莫不羡其风。

translations.literal: At the time guests filled the hall—none did not admire his air.
translations.idiomatic: Guests packed the room and envied his bearing.

sentences.zh: 府掾孔融、王朗并修刺候焉。

translations.literal: Office aides Kong Rong and Wang Lang both presented cards and called on him.
translations.idiomatic: Staff aides Kong Rong and Wang Lang sent visiting cards and paid their respects.

sentences.zh: 议郎蔡邕深敬之，以为让宜处高任，乃荐于何进曰：

translations.literal: Gentleman Consultant Cai Yong deeply revered him—thought Rang suited high office—thereupon recommended to He Jin saying:
translations.idiomatic: Gentleman Cai Yong esteemed him, held that Rang deserved rank, and wrote He Jin:

sentences.zh: 伏惟幕府初开，博选清英，华发旧德，并为元鬼。

translations.literal: I humbly reflect: your headquarters newly opens—you broadly choose pure talents—gray-haired elders of virtue stand as chief oracle counselors.
translations.idiomatic: Your new command gathers brilliant men; hoary worthies serve as your council of sages.

sentences.zh: 虽振鹭之集西雍，济济之在周庭，无以或加。

translations.literal: Though egrets gather at western Yong—crowded in Zhou's court—nothing could surpass this.
translations.idiomatic: Like herons flocking to the western pond or the throng in Zhou's hall—none finer.

sentences.zh: 窃见令史陈留边让，天授逸才，聪明贤智。

translations.literal: I have observed clerk Bian Rang of Chenliu—Heaven granted him roaming genius—bright, worthy, wise.
translations.idiomatic: Your clerk Bian Rang of Chenliu bears Heaven's genius—lucid, good, wise.

sentences.zh: 髫齓夙孤，不盡家訓。

translations.literal: Orphaned in childhood, he did not receive the full instruction of his family.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned as a child, he never received his family's full training.

sentences.zh: 及就学庐，便受大典。

translations.literal: When he entered the study hall—he received the great canons.
translations.idiomatic: Once in school he mastered the great classics.

sentences.zh: 初涉诸经，见本知义。

translations.literal: First treading the classics—seeing root he knew meaning.
translations.idiomatic: At first touch of each classic he saw root meaning.

sentences.zh: 授者不能对其问，章句不能逮其意。

translations.literal: Teachers could not answer his questions—glosses could not reach his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Tutors could not meet his questions; chapter glosses could not catch his sense.

sentences.zh: 心通性達，口辯辭長。

translations.literal: If he is again advanced only along with his peers, that is not how to make manifest the high worth of extraordinary greatness, or display peerless clarity in knowing men.
translations.idiomatic: If he rises only with the crowd, his rare worth will not be made plain, nor will your unmatched eye for talent.

sentences.zh: 非禮不動，非法不言。

translations.literal: If he is again advanced only along with his peers, that is not how to make manifest the high worth of extraordinary greatness, or display peerless clarity in knowing men.
translations.idiomatic: If he rises only with the crowd, his rare worth will not be made plain, nor will your unmatched eye for talent.

sentences.zh: 若處狐疑之論，定嫌審之分，經典交至，撿括參合，眾夫寂焉，莫之能奪也。

translations.literal: If he is again advanced only along with his peers, that is not how to make manifest the high worth of extraordinary greatness, or display peerless clarity in knowing men.
translations.idiomatic: If he rises only with the crowd, his rare worth will not be made plain, nor will your unmatched eye for talent.

sentences.zh: 使讓生在唐、虞，則元、凱之次，運値仲尼，則顔、冉之亞，豈徒俗之凡偶近器而已者哉！

translations.literal: If he is again advanced only along with his peers, that is not how to make manifest the high worth of extraordinary greatness, or display peerless clarity in knowing men.
translations.idiomatic: If he rises only with the crowd, his rare worth will not be made plain, nor will your unmatched eye for talent.

sentences.zh: 階級名位，亦宜超然。

translations.literal: If he is again advanced only along with his peers, that is not how to make manifest the high worth of extraordinary greatness, or display peerless clarity in knowing men.
translations.idiomatic: If he rises only with the crowd, his rare worth will not be made plain, nor will your unmatched eye for talent.

sentences.zh: 若復隨輩而進，非所以章瑰偉之高價，昭知人之絶明也。

translations.literal: If he is again advanced only along with his peers, that is not how to make manifest the high worth of extraordinary greatness, or display peerless clarity in knowing men.
translations.idiomatic: If he rises only with the crowd, his rare worth will not be made plain, nor will your unmatched eye for talent.

sentences.zh: 傳曰：「函牛之鼎以亨雞，多汁則淡而不可食，少計則熬而不可熟。」

translations.literal: If he is again advanced only along with his peers, that is not how to make manifest the high worth of extraordinary greatness, or display peerless clarity in knowing men.
translations.idiomatic: If he rises only with the crowd, his rare worth will not be made plain, nor will your unmatched eye for talent.

sentences.zh: 此言大器之于小用，固有所不宜也。

translations.literal: This speaks of great vessels used for petty tasks—indeed some uses do not fit.
translations.idiomatic: That is great gear forced to small jobs—some fits will always fail.

sentences.zh: 邕竊悁邑，怪此寶鼎未受犧牛大羹之和，久在煎熬臠割之間。

translations.literal: I, Yong, am privately distressed, wondering that this precious cauldron has not received the blending of sacrificial ox and great soup, but has long remained amid boiling and slicing.
translations.idiomatic: I am pained that such a precious vessel has never been put to grand sacrificial use, but has long languished among petty boiling and carving.

sentences.zh: 願明將軍回謀垂慮，裁加少納，貢之機密，展之力用。

translations.literal: I, Yong, am privately distressed, wondering that this precious cauldron has not received the blending of sacrificial ox and great soup, but has long remained amid boiling and slicing.
translations.idiomatic: I am pained that such a precious vessel has never been put to grand sacrificial use, but has long languished among petty boiling and carving.

sentences.zh: 若以年齒爲嫌，則顔回不得貫德行之首，子奇終無理阿之功。

translations.literal: I, Yong, am privately distressed, wondering that this precious cauldron has not received the blending of sacrificial ox and great soup, but has long remained amid boiling and slicing.
translations.idiomatic: I am pained that such a precious vessel has never been put to grand sacrificial use, but has long languished among petty boiling and carving.

sentences.zh: 苟堪其事，古今一也。

translations.literal: If he can bear the task—ancient and modern are one.
translations.idiomatic: If he can do the work, old rule and new are the same.

sentences.zh: 讓後以高才擢進，屢遷，出爲九江太守，不以爲能也。

translations.literal: Rang later by high talent was promoted—often transferred—went out as Jiujiang governor—did not think himself able.
translations.idiomatic: Rang rose on talent through many posts and became Jiujiang governor—yet still doubted his worth.

sentences.zh: 初平中，王室大亂，讓去官還家。

translations.literal: In Chuping the royal house fell into chaos—Rang left office and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: When Chuping broke the court he resigned and went home.

sentences.zh: 恃才氣，不屈曹操，多輕侮之言。

translations.literal: He trusted his gifts—would not bend to Cao Cao—often spoke slightingly.
translations.idiomatic: He leaned on his wit, refused Cao Cao, and often mocked him.

sentences.zh: 建安中，其乡人有构让于操，操告郡就杀之。

translations.literal: Under Jian'an a fellow villager framed Rang to Cao—Cao told the commandery to kill him on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: In Jian'an a townsman slandered him; Cao ordered the commandery to execute him there.

sentences.zh: 文多遗失。

translations.literal: His writings are largely lost.
translations.idiomatic: Most of his writings are gone.

sentences.zh: 酈炎字文勝，范陽人，酈食其之後也。

translations.literal: Li Yan courtesy Wensheng—a man of Fanyang—descendant of Li Yiji.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yan, styled Wensheng, from Fanyang, line of Li Yiji.

sentences.zh: 炎有文才，解音律，言論給捷，多服其能理。

translations.literal: Yan had literary talent—understood pitch pipes—speech quick—many admired his clear reasoning.
translations.idiomatic: Yan wrote well, knew music, spoke with wit, and men praised his sense.

sentences.zh: 灵帝时，州郡辟命，皆不就，有志气。

translations.literal: Under Lingdi provinces and commanderies summoned—he accepted none—he had backbone.
translations.idiomatic: Lingdi's era brought offers from every office—all refused—he had spine.

sentences.zh: 作诗二篇曰：

translations.literal: He composed two poems saying:
translations.idiomatic: He wrote two poems:

sentences.zh: 大道夷且长，窘路狭且促。

translations.literal: The great way is level and long—the strait path narrow and tight.
translations.idiomatic: The broad road runs smooth and far; the trapdoor track is narrow and short.

sentences.zh: 修冀无卑栖，远趾不步局。

translations.literal: Long pinions will not roost low—far strides will not pace a cage.
translations.idiomatic: Great wings do not perch low; wide steps do not pace a pen.

sentences.zh: 舒吾陵霄羽，奋此千里足。

translations.literal: I spread my sky-piercing wings—I spur these thousand-mile hooves.
translations.idiomatic: I spread wings to vault heaven; I spur these thousand-mile legs.

sentences.zh: 超邁絶塵驅，倏忽誰能逐。

translations.literal: Surpassing the dust-raised drive, in a sudden instant who could pursue?
translations.idiomatic: I race beyond the dust; in a flash no one can catch me.

sentences.zh: 賢愚豈常類，稟性在清濁。

translations.literal: How could worthy and foolish be fixed kinds? Endowed nature lies in clarity or turbidity.
translations.idiomatic: Worth and folly are not fixed castes; they depend on the clarity or murk of one's nature.

sentences.zh: 富貴有人籍，貧賤無天錄。

translations.literal: Wealth and honor have human registers; poverty and lowliness have no record from Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Ranks of wealth are written by men; poverty has no warrant from Heaven.

sentences.zh: 通塞苟由已，志士不相卜。

translations.literal: Open or blocked—if from oneself—resolute men cast no lots.
translations.idiomatic: Success lies with the self—the steadfast do not augur each other.

sentences.zh: 陳平敖里社，韓信釣河曲。

translations.literal: Chen Ping boasted at the village altar—Han Xin angled in the river bend.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Ping strutted at the village altar; Han Xin fished the river curve.

sentences.zh: 終居天下宰，食此萬鍾祿。

translations.literal: In the end they held the ministries of all under Heaven and ate stipends of ten thousand zhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the end they governed the empire on ten-thousand-measure stipends.

sentences.zh: 德音流千載，功名重山岳。

translations.literal: Virtuous fame flows a thousand ages—merit and name weigh like peaks.
translations.idiomatic: Their names echo forever; their deeds outweigh mountains.

sentences.zh: 靈芝生河洲，動搖因洪波。

translations.literal: Magic fungus grows on the river isle—it trembles in the vast flood.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit fungus on the midstream bar shivers in the surge.

sentences.zh: 蘭榮一何晚，嚴霜瘁其柯。

translations.literal: How late the orchid flowered; harsh frost withered its branch.
translations.idiomatic: The orchid bloomed too late, and bitter frost withered its stem.

sentences.zh: 哀哉二芳草，不植太山阿。

translations.literal: Alas the two fragrant grasses—not planted on Taishan's slope.
translations.idiomatic: Alas—two sweet orchids never took root on Tai's shoulder.

sentences.zh: 文質道所貴，遭時用有嘉。

translations.literal: When Zhou Bo of Jiang and Guan Ying occupied the chief ministerial posts, they said Jia Yi exalted empty ornament.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Bo and Guan Ying held power, they dismissed Jia Yi as a lover of hollow brilliance.

sentences.zh: 絳、灌臨衡宰，謂誼崇浮華。

translations.literal: When Zhou Bo of Jiang and Guan Ying occupied the chief ministerial posts, they said Jia Yi exalted empty ornament.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Bo and Guan Ying held power, they dismissed Jia Yi as a lover of hollow brilliance.

sentences.zh: 贤才抑不用，远投荆南沙。

translations.literal: Worthy talent suppressed unused—cast far to southern Jing sands.
translations.idiomatic: The worthy were blocked and banished to the southern waste.

sentences.zh: 抱玉乘龙骥，不逢乐与和。

translations.literal: He clasped jade and rode dragon steeds—met neither music nor harmony.
translations.idiomatic: He bore his gem astride a swift mount yet heard no tune that fit.

sentences.zh: 安得孔仲尼，为世陈四科。

translations.literal: How gain Kong Zhongni—to lay out for the age the four categories?
translations.idiomatic: Where is a Confucius to set the four classes for this age?

sentences.zh: 炎後風病慌忽。

translations.literal: His wife had just given birth when she was frightened to death; her family sued him, and he was arrested and held in prison.
translations.idiomatic: His wife was frightened to death just after childbirth; her family sued, and he was jailed.

sentences.zh: 性至孝，遭母憂，病甚發動。

translations.literal: His wife had just given birth when she was frightened to death; her family sued him, and he was arrested and held in prison.
translations.idiomatic: His wife was frightened to death just after childbirth; her family sued, and he was jailed.

sentences.zh: 妻始産而驚死，妻家訟之，收繫獄。

translations.literal: His wife had just given birth when she was frightened to death; her family sued him, and he was arrested and held in prison.
translations.idiomatic: His wife was frightened to death just after childbirth; her family sued, and he was jailed.

sentences.zh: 炎病不能理对，嘉平六年，遂死狱中，时年二十八。

translations.literal: Yan ill could not manage replies—sixth year Jiaping—thereupon died in prison—age twenty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Too sick to speak in court, he perished in jail in Jiaping 6 at twenty-eight.

sentences.zh: 尙書盧植爲之誄贊，以昭其懿德。

translations.literal: Director Lu Zhi composed dirge-praise for him—to display his excellent virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Lu Zhi wrote his elegy to publish his fine conduct.

sentences.zh: 侯瑾字子瑜，敦煌人也。

translations.literal: Hou Jin courtesy Ziyu—a man of Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jin, styled Ziyu, came from Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 少孤贫，依宗人居。

translations.literal: Youth orphaned and poor—relied on kin to dwell.
translations.idiomatic: Fatherless and poor as a boy, he lodged with relatives.

sentences.zh: 性篤學，恆傭作爲資，暮還輒燃柴以讀書。

translations.literal: Nature earnest in study—always hired labor for funds—returning at dusk he burned brushwood to read.
translations.idiomatic: He studied with fierce zeal, hired himself out by day, and by night burned kindling to read.

sentences.zh: 常以礼自牧，独处一房，如对严宾焉。

translations.literal: Constantly by ritual he governed himself—dwelt alone in one chamber—as facing stern guests.
translations.idiomatic: He kept ritual discipline alone in his room as though honored guests sat with him.

sentences.zh: 州郡累召，公車有道徵，幷稱疾不到。

translations.idiomatic: He once sought Ma Rong's teaching on the great principles, but Rong was ill and would not see him. Gao Biao then sent in a card and left a letter: "I have admired your reputation for years, and came without a go-between to the gate of a great gentleman, hoping for one glimpse of your radiance and a chance to speak my heart.

translations.literal: Did not expect to meet illness—gates barred unopened.
translations.idiomatic: He never meant to find sickness—doors stayed shut.

sentences.zh: 昔周公旦父文兄武，九命作伯，以尹華夏，猶揮沐吐餐，垂接白屋，故周道以隆，天下歸德。

translations.literal: Anciently Duke of Zhou—father Wen elder brother Wu—nine commands made Earl—to rule Huaxia—still wrung dripping hair and spat mid-meal—to receive common-roof men—therefore Zhou's Way rose—all under Heaven returned to virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Zhou ruled between father Wen and brother Wu with nine honors—yet washed his hair mid-bath and spat out food to meet poor scholars—so Zhou flourished and the world turned kind.

sentences.zh: 公今養疴傲士，故其宜也。」

translations.literal: Sir today nurtures illness and scorns scholars—that suits your case."
translations.idiomatic: Today you nurse sickness and scorn visitors—that fits you.

sentences.zh: 融省書慚，追謝還之，彪逝而不顧。

translations.literal: Rong read the letter and was ashamed; he pursued Biao to apologize and bring him back, but Biao went away without looking back.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Rong read the letter in shame and hurried after him to apologize, but Biao left without looking back.

sentences.zh: 後郡舉孝廉，試經第一。

translations.literal: Later commandery raised him filial and incorrupt—classics exam ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery nominated him filial-incorrupt; he topped the classics test.

sentences.zh: 除郎中，校書東觀。

translations.literal: He was appointed Gentleman Attendant and collated books in the Eastern Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Gentleman Attendant and set to collating texts in the Eastern Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 數奏賦、頌、奇文，因事諷諫，靈帝異之。

translations.literal: He repeatedly submitted fu, eulogies, and unusual writings, using events to remonstrate by indirection, and Emperor Ling regarded him as exceptional.
translations.idiomatic: Again and again he submitted rhapsodies and essays that used current events for indirect remonstrance, and Emperor Ling took notice.

sentences.zh: 時，京兆第五永爲督軍御史，使督幽州。

translations.literal: At the time Capital District Diwu Yong was Supervising Army Censor—sent to oversee Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Diwu Yong of the capital served as army censor over Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 百官大會，祖餞於長樂觀。

translations.literal: The hundred officials assembled in a great gathering and held farewell rites at Changle Lodge.
translations.idiomatic: The officials gathered in force to send him off with a farewell banquet at Changle Lodge.

sentences.zh: 議郎葵邑等皆賦詩，彪乃獨作箴曰：「文武將墜，乃俾俊臣。

translations.literal: Gentleman Consultant Cai Yong and others all composed verse—Biao alone wrote admonition saying: "Civil and martial about to fall—thereupon entrust fine ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yong and the rest wrote poems; Biao alone offered a warning: when arms and letters waver, send worthy men.

sentences.zh: 整我皇纲，董此不虔。

translations.literal: Set our royal net straight—oversee this irreverence.
translations.idiomatic: Straighten the imperial cords and watch the faithless.

sentences.zh: 古之君子，即戎忘身。

translations.literal: Ancient gentlemen—took up arms forgot self.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient nobles forgot themselves once they bore arms.

sentences.zh: 明其果毅，尚其桓桓。

translations.literal: Make plain their resolve and courage—honor their stern stride.
translations.idiomatic: Make firm resolve clear and praise their grim march.

sentences.zh: 呂尙七十，氣冠三軍，詩人作歌，如鷹如鸇。

translations.literal: Lü Shang was seventy, yet his spirit overtopped the three armies; the poet made a song, likening him to a hawk and a harrier.
translations.idiomatic: At seventy, Lü Shang's vigor still towered over the armies; poets sang of him as hawk and harrier.

sentences.zh: 天有太一，五將三門；

translations.literal: Lü Shang was seventy, yet his spirit overtopped the three armies; the poet made a song, likening him to a hawk and a harrier.
translations.idiomatic: At seventy, Lü Shang's vigor still towered over the armies; poets sang of him as hawk and harrier.

sentences.zh: 地有九变，丘陵山川；

translations.literal: Earth has nine transformations—mounds hills rivers streams;
translations.idiomatic: Earth shifts nine ways—hill and stream.

sentences.zh: 人有计策，六奇五间。

translations.literal: Men have stratagems—six marvels five spies.
translations.idiomatic: Men wield plots—six wonders and five infiltrators.

sentences.zh: 總茲三事，謀則咨詢。

translations.literal: Gather these three matters together, and when planning, consult others.
translations.idiomatic: Hold these three together, and take counsel before you plan.

sentences.zh: 無曰己能，務在求賢，淮陰之勇，廣野是尊。

translations.literal: Say not "I alone am able"—seek worth must be the task—Huaiyin's valor—Wilderness Plain revered.
translations.idiomatic: Never boast sole wisdom—seek sages—remember Huaiyin's courage at Wild Goose Marsh.

sentences.zh: 周公大聖，石碏純臣，以威克愛，以義滅親。

translations.literal: The Duke of Zhou was a great sage, and Shi Que a pure minister; with stern authority they overcame affection, and with righteousness they put kin to death.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Zhou was sage and Shi Que pure; severity overcame affection, and duty overrode kinship.

sentences.zh: 勿謂時險，不正其身。

translations.literal: Say not times treacherous—fail to straighten self.
translations.idiomatic: Never blame dark times for crooked conduct.

sentences.zh: 勿謂無人，莫識己眞。

translations.literal: Do not say there is no one and that none knows your true self.
translations.idiomatic: Do not say no one is watching, or that no one knows your true self.

sentences.zh: 忘富遺貴，福祿乃存。

translations.literal: Forget wealth and leave rank behind; only then do blessing and stipend endure.
translations.idiomatic: Forget riches and rank, and only then will fortune last.

sentences.zh: 枉道依合，復無所觀。

translations.literal: Crook path to curry favor—again nothing to see.
translations.idiomatic: Twist principle to please—and merit is hollow.

sentences.zh: 先公高节，越可永遵。

translations.literal: Former lord high integrity—Yue may forever follow.
translations.idiomatic: Your father's stern virtue is the pattern forever.

sentences.zh: 佩藏斯戒，以厲終身。」

translations.literal: Wear hidden this warning—to spur whole life."
translations.idiomatic: Keep this lesson pinned—to steel a lifetime.

sentences.zh: 邕等甚美其文，以为莫尚也。

translations.literal: Yong and others greatly praised its writing—thought none surpassed.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yong and company praised the piece above all others.

sentences.zh: 後遷外黃令，帝敕同僚臨送，祖於上東門，詔東觀畫彪像以勸學者。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to be magistrate of Waihuang; the emperor ordered his colleagues to attend his send-off and perform the farewell rite at the Upper East Gate, and commanded the Eastern Pavilion to paint Biao's portrait to encourage students.
translations.idiomatic: When he was later moved to Waihuang, the emperor ordered his colleagues to see him off at the Upper East Gate and had the Eastern Pavilion paint his portrait as an example for students.

sentences.zh: 彪到官，有德政，上書薦縣人申徒蟠等。
