sentences.zh: 病卒于官，文章多亡。

translations.literal: Died of illness in post—writings largely lost.
translations.idiomatic: He died in harness; most of his works vanished.

sentences.zh: 子岱，亦知名。

translations.literal: Son Dai—also gained fame.
translations.idiomatic: His son Dai won renown too.

sentences.zh: 張超字子幷，河間鄚人也，留侯良之後也。

translations.literal: Zhang Chao courtesy Zibing—a man of Mo in Hejian—descendant of Marquis Liu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chao, styled Zibing, from Mo in Hejian, line of Marquis Zhang Liang.

sentences.zh: 有文才。

translations.literal: Had literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote with skill.

sentences.zh: 靈帝時，從車騎將軍朱雋徵黃巾，爲別部司馬。

translations.literal: Under Lingdi followed chariot-and-horse general Zhu Jun against Yellow Turbans—as separate division major.
translations.idiomatic: Under Lingdi he rode with Zhu Jun against the turbans as an independent major.

sentences.zh: 著賦、頌、碑文、薦、檄、箋、書、謁文、嘲，凡十九篇。

translations.literal: Composed fu, eulogies, stele texts, recommendations, proclamations, notes, letters, visiting cards, jeers—nineteen pieces in all.
translations.idiomatic: Nineteen pieces survive: rhapsodies, eulogies, steles, recommendations, calls, notes, letters, cards, and lampoons.

sentences.zh: 超又善於草書，妙絶時人，世共傳之。

translations.literal: Chao also skilled at cursive script—wondrous beyond his age—all generations transmit.
translations.idiomatic: His grass script was unmatched and copied everywhere.

sentences.zh: 禰衡字正平，平原般人也。

translations.literal: Mi Heng courtesy Zhengping—a man of Ban in Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Mi Heng, styled Zhengping, came from Ban in Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 少有才辯，而尙氣剛傲，好矯時慢物。

translations.literal: Youth had eloquence and wit—yet prized temper proud—loved correcting age and scorning things.
translations.idiomatic: Young, sharp-tongued and proud, he delighted in defying fashion and sneering at the great.

sentences.zh: 興平中，避難荆州。

translations.literal: Xingping middle—fled trouble to Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Xingping he fled turmoil to Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 建安初，來遊許下。

translations.literal: Jian'an early—came wandering to Xu below.
translations.idiomatic: Early Jian'an brought him to the court at Xu.

sentences.zh: 始達潁川，乃陰懷一剌，旣而無所之適，至於刺字漫滅。

translations.literal: First reaching Yingchuan—secretly hugged one visiting card—yet nowhere to go—until card letters wore away.
translations.idiomatic: In Yingchuan he hid a name card until no door took him and the ink rubbed bare.

sentences.zh: 是時，許都新建，賢士大夫，四方來集。

translations.literal: At that time capital Xu newly built—worthy officials and gentry—from four quarters gathered.
translations.idiomatic: Xu was new then; talent flooded in from every quarter.

sentences.zh: 或問衡曰：「盍從陳長文、司馬伯達乎？」

translations.literal: Someone asked Heng: "Why not follow Chen Zhangwen and Sima Boda?"
translations.idiomatic: They asked, "Why not follow Chen Ji or Sima Lang?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「吾焉能從屠沽兒耶！」

translations.literal: Answered: "How could I follow butcher and wine-boy brats!"
translations.idiomatic: He shot back, "Why would I trail tavern louts and butchers' sons!"

sentences.zh: 又问：“荀文若、赵稚长云何？”

translations.literal: Again asked: "What of Xun Wenruo and Zhao Zhichang?"
translations.idiomatic: They pressed, "What of Xun Yu and Zhao Zhi then?"

sentences.zh: 衡曰：“文若可借面吊丧，稚长可使监厨请客。”

translations.literal: Heng said: "Wenruo could lend face for mourning—Zhichang could supervise kitchen feasts."
translations.idiomatic: He sneered that Xun Yu had only a face fit for funerals and Zhao Zhi for catering.

sentences.zh: 唯善鲁国孔融及弘农杨脩。

translations.literal: Only favored Kong Rong of Lu and Yang Xiu of Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: He granted only Kong Rong and Yang Xiu.

sentences.zh: 常称曰：“大兒孔文举，小兒杨德祖。

translations.literal: Often declared: "Eldest son Kong Wenju—youngest son Yang Dezu.
translations.idiomatic: He called Kong Rong the elder twin star and Yang Xiu the younger.

sentences.zh: 余子碌碌，莫足数也。”

translations.literal: Other sons dull—not worth counting."
translations.idiomatic: The rest were straw—not worth naming.

sentences.zh: 融亦深爱其才。

translations.literal: Rong also deeply loved his talent.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Rong adored his gift.

sentences.zh: 衡始弱冠，而融年四十，遂与为交友。

translations.literal: Heng just capped twenty—Rong age forty—thereupon became friends.
translations.idiomatic: Heng was barely twenty when forty-year-old Rong befriended him.

sentences.zh: 上疏薦之曰：臣聞洪水橫流，帝思俾乂，旁求四方，以招賢俊。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial recommending him, saying: "Your servant has heard that when the floodwaters ran wild, the emperor thought to bring order and searched widely through the four quarters to summon the worthy and outstanding.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial recommending him: "I have heard that when the floods spread, the emperor sought order by searching the realm for worthy men.

sentences.zh: 昔孝武繼統，將弘祖業，疇咨熙載，群士響臻。

translations.literal: In former times, when Emperor Xiaowu inherited the succession and was about to enlarge his ancestral enterprise, he consulted broadly to make the work bright, and many scholars came in response.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu took up the line and enlarged his ancestors' work, he sought counsel, and scholars flocked to him.

sentences.zh: 陛下睿聖，纂承基緒，遭遇厄運，勞謙日昃。

translations.literal: Your Majesty wise and holy—inherits foundation—meets dark fortune—laboring humble past noon.
translations.idiomatic: You are keen of mind yet inherit crisis and toil past sundown.

sentences.zh: 惟岳降神，異人幷出。

translations.literal: Peak sends spirits—strange men emerge together.
translations.idiomatic: The sacred peak sends spirits—talents rise together.

sentences.zh: 竊見處士平原禰衡，年二十四，字正平，淑質貞亮，英才卓礫。

translations.literal: I have privately observed the private scholar Mi Heng of Pingyuan, aged twenty-four, courtesy name Zhengping; his fine substance is upright and bright, and his brilliant talent is outstanding.
translations.idiomatic: I have observed Mi Heng of Pingyuan, a private scholar of twenty-four styled Zhengping: his nature is pure and bright, his talent extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 初涉藝文，昇堂睹奧。

translations.literal: First treading arts and letters—entered hall and saw inner shrine.
translations.idiomatic: Touching the classics he reached their inner rooms.

sentences.zh: 目所一見，輒誦於口；

translations.literal: Whatever his eyes see once, he immediately recites from his mouth;
translations.idiomatic: Whatever he sees once, he can recite at once;

sentences.zh: 耳所瞥闻，不忘于心。

translations.literal: What ear once brushed—does not fade from heart.
translations.idiomatic: One whisper lodged in memory.

sentences.zh: 性与道合，思若有神。

translations.literal: Nature joins the Way—thought as though spirit.
translations.idiomatic: His nature meets the Way—thought moves like spirit.

sentences.zh: 弘羊潛計，安世默識，以衡準之，誠不足怪。

translations.literal: Sang Hongyang's hidden sums—Zhang Anshi's silent reckoning—measured against Heng—indeed not strange.
translations.idiomatic: Against Sang Hongyang's sums or Zhang Anshi's memory he is no marvel less.

sentences.zh: 忠果正直，志怀霜雪。

translations.literal: Loyal firm upright—intent holds frost and snow.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal and blunt—his will is frost.

sentences.zh: 見善若驚，疾惡若仇。

translations.literal: He sees good as if startled, and hates evil as an enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Good startles him; evil he treats as a sworn enemy.

sentences.zh: 任座抗行，史魚厲節，殆無以過也。

translations.literal: Ren Zuo's stiff courage—Shi Yu's fierce integrity—hardly surpass.
translations.idiomatic: He rivals Ren Zuo's blunt truth and the historian's steel.

sentences.zh: 鷙鳥累伯，不如一鶚。

translations.literal: Hundreds of fierce birds are not equal to one osprey.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred raptors are worth less than one osprey.

sentences.zh: 使衡立朝，必有可觀。

translations.literal: Were Heng to stand at court—surely worth viewing.
translations.idiomatic: Set him in court and the realm would see.

sentences.zh: 飛辯騁辭，溢氣坌涌，解疑釋結，臨敵有餘。

translations.literal: Flying debate racing phrases—breath overflows—unravels doubt unties knots—facing foes abundant.
translations.idiomatic: His words scatter fog and cut knots—enough for any foe.

sentences.zh: 昔賈誼求試屬國，詭繫單於；

translations.literal: Formerly Jia Yi asked to be tested in a dependent-state post, to bind the Chanyu by stratagem;
translations.idiomatic: Jia Yi once sought a frontier post to snare the Chanyu by stratagem;

sentences.zh: 終軍欲以長纓，牽致勁越。

translations.literal: Zhong Jun wished to use a long cord to draw in powerful Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Jun wanted to bring fierce Yue in on a long cord.

sentences.zh: 弱冠慷慨，前世美之。

translations.literal: Weak-capped fervor—past ages praised.
translations.idiomatic: Youth that bold—history praised.

sentences.zh: 近日路粹、嚴象，亦用異才，擢拜臺郎，衡宜與爲比。

translations.literal: In the vast music of Juntian, there must be wondrous and beautiful sights;
translations.idiomatic: The celestial music of Juntian must surely hold wonders of beauty;

sentences.zh: 如得龍躍天衢，振翼雲漢，揚聲紫微，垂光虹蜺，足以昭近署之多士，增四門之穆穆。

translations.literal: In the vast music of Juntian, there must be wondrous and beautiful sights;
translations.idiomatic: The celestial music of Juntian must surely hold wonders of beauty;

sentences.zh: 鈞天廣樂，必有奇麗之觀；

translations.literal: In the vast music of Juntian, there must be wondrous and beautiful sights;
translations.idiomatic: The celestial music of Juntian must surely hold wonders of beauty;

sentences.zh: 帝室皇居，必蓄非常之宝。

translations.literal: Imperial house august dwelling—surely stores extraordinary treasures.
translations.idiomatic: The throne hoards gems beyond the common.

sentences.zh: 若衡等輩，不可多得。

translations.literal: Men like Heng cannot be had in clusters.
translations.idiomatic: Talent like Mi Heng rarely appears twice in an age.

sentences.zh: 《激楚》、《楊阿》，至妙之容，臺牧者之所貪；

translations.literal: "Ji Chu" and "Yang E"—supreme grace—what terrace patrons crave;
translations.idiomatic: The airs "Ji Chu" and "Yang E" hold the finest charm—exactly what idle hosts hoard.

sentences.zh: 飛兔、騕褭，絶足奔放，良、樂之所急。

translations.literal: Flying Hare and Yaoniao—hooves unmatched—what Boy Ya and Le raced to seize.
translations.idiomatic: Steeds like Flying Hare and Yaoniao—fleet beyond measure—the mounts Bo Le prized.

sentences.zh: 臣等區區，敢不以聞。

translations.literal: We petty servants dare not withhold report.
translations.idiomatic: Your servants humbly dare not leave this unsaid.

sentences.zh: 融旣愛衡才，數稱述於曹操。

translations.literal: Rong loving Heng's talent repeatedly praised him to Cao Cao.
translations.idiomatic: Because Kong Rong prized Mi Heng he spoke of him again and again to Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 操欲見之，而衡素相輕疾，自稱狂病，不肯往，而數有恣言。

translations.literal: Cao wished to see him—yet Heng always despised him—called himself mad—refused to go—and kept reckless speech.
translations.idiomatic: Cao wanted an audience; Mi Heng loathed him, feigned madness, stayed away, and kept firing insults.

sentences.zh: 操怀忿，而以其才名，不欲杀之。

translations.literal: Cao nursed wrath—yet for his talent's fame—would not kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Cao burned with anger yet spared him for the sake of his reputation.

sentences.zh: 聞衡善擊鼓，乃召爲鼓史，因大會賓客，閲試音節。

translations.literal: Hearing Heng excelled at drums—summoned him drum clerk—thereupon great assembly of guests—to test rhythm.
translations.idiomatic: Learning Mi Heng's skill on the drum, Cao named him drum clerk and threw a banquet to hear him.

sentences.zh: 諸史過者，皆令脫其故衣，更著岑牟、單絞之服。

translations.literal: All clerks passing were ordered strip old clothes—don drum-cap and thin jacket.
translations.idiomatic: Every drummer had to shed his clothes for the uniform cap and jacket.

sentences.zh: 次至衡，衡方爲《漁陽》參撾，蹀𨄌而前，容態有異，聲節悲壯，聽者莫不慷慨。

translations.literal: When the turn came to Heng, Heng was then beating the triple strokes of “Yuyang”; stepping forward, his bearing was unusual and the rhythm mournfully vigorous, so none who heard it failed to be stirred.
translations.idiomatic: When Mi Heng’s turn came, he struck the “Yuyang” triple beat and stepped forward, his bearing strange and the rhythm fierce with grief; everyone listening was moved.

sentences.zh: 衡進至操前而止，吏呵之曰：「鼓史何不改裝，而輕敢進乎？」

translations.literal: Heng advanced before Cao and stopped—clerk shouted: "Drum clerk why not change dress—dare advance rashly?"
translations.idiomatic: Mi Heng walked up to Cao Cao and halted; a clerk barked, "Why keep your old clothes—how dare you step up like that?"

sentences.zh: 衡曰：「諾。」

translations.literal: When the turn came to Heng, Heng was then beating the triple strokes of “Yuyang”; stepping forward, his bearing was unusual and the rhythm mournfully vigorous, so none who heard it failed to be stirred.
translations.idiomatic: When Mi Heng’s turn came, he struck the “Yuyang” triple beat and stepped forward, his bearing strange and the rhythm fierce with grief; everyone listening was moved.

sentences.zh: 於是先解衵衣，次釋餘服，裸身而立，徐取岑牟、單絞而著之，畢，復參撾而去，顔色不怍。

translations.literal: Thereupon first shed inner shirt—next shed remaining—stood naked—slowly took drum-cap thin jacket and donned—finished—again triple-drummed and departed—face unashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Then he stripped his undershirt, shed the rest, stood bare, slowly pulled on cap and jacket, finished the triple roll, and walked off without a blush.

sentences.zh: 操笑曰：“本欲辱衡，衡反辱孤。”

translations.literal: Cao laughed: "I meant to shame Heng—Heng shames me instead.
translations.idiomatic: Cao laughed. "I meant to humiliate him—he humiliated me."

sentences.zh: 孔融退而数之曰：“正平大雅，固当尔邪？”

translations.literal: Kong Rong withdrew and scolded him: "Zhengping you claim high style—is this how it looks?"
translations.idiomatic: Kong Rong pulled him aside: "You call yourself refined—is this what you call fitting?"

sentences.zh: 因宣操区区之意。

translations.literal: Thereupon declared Cao's humble intent.
translations.idiomatic: Then he relayed Cao Cao's conciliatory message.

sentences.zh: 衡许往。

translations.literal: Heng promised to go.
translations.idiomatic: Mi Heng agreed to call.

sentences.zh: 融复见操，说衡狂疾，今求得自谢。

translations.literal: Rong again saw Cao—said Heng's madness—now seeks self apology.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Rong told Cao the madness had passed and Mi Heng wished to apologize in person.

sentences.zh: 操喜，敕门者有客便通，待之极晏。

translations.literal: Cao pleased—ordered gate any guest admit—waited very late.
translations.idiomatic: Cao was delighted and told the gate to admit anyone at once; he waited deep into the evening.

sentences.zh: 衡乃着布单衣、疏巾，手持三尺棁杖，坐大营门，以杖捶地大骂。

translations.literal: Heng wore plain robe loose kerchief—held three-foot rod—sat great camp gate—beat earth with rod and cursed.
translations.idiomatic: Mi Heng came in plain cloth and loose scarf, gripped a three-foot rod, sat at the camp gate, drummed the ground with it, and roared abuse.

sentences.zh: 吏曰：“外有狂生，坐于营门，言语悖逆，请收案罪。”

translations.literal: Clerk said: "Outside mad scholar sits camp gate—speech rebellious—please seize for crime."
translations.idiomatic: An aide reported, "A madman sits at the gate hurling treason—arrest him."

sentences.zh: 操怒，谓融曰：“祢衡竖子，孤杀之犹雀鼠耳。

translations.literal: Cao angry told Rong: "Mi Heng brat—I kill him like sparrow mouse.
translations.idiomatic: Cao snapped at Kong Rong, "That wretch Mi Heng—I could crush him like a bug."

sentences.zh: 顾此人素有虚名，远近将谓孤不能容之，今送与刘表，视当何如。”

translations.literal: Yet this man has empty fame—near far will say I cannot bear him—now send to Liu Biao—see how it goes."
translations.idiomatic: Yet he has a hollow reputation; if I kill him every mouth will say I cannot abide counsel—pack him off to Liu Biao and watch what happens.

sentences.zh: 于是遣人骑送之。

translations.literal: Thereupon sent riders escort him.
translations.idiomatic: So Cao had horsemen escort him away.

sentences.zh: 临发，众人为之祖道，先供设于城南，乃更相戒曰：“祢衡勃虐无礼，今因其后到，咸当以不起折之也。”

translations.literal: Before departure crowd farewelled him—first set feast south city—mutually warned: "Mi Heng cruel rude—now because he comes late—all should refuse rise to humble him."
translations.idiomatic: They staged a send-off south of the city and agreed that because Mi Heng was crude and late they would all stay seated to humble him.

sentences.zh: 及衡至，众人莫肯兴，衡坐而大号。

translations.literal: When Heng arrived—none would rise—Heng sat and wailed loud.
translations.idiomatic: When he came nobody stood; Mi Heng sat down and howled.

sentences.zh: 众问其故，衡曰：“坐者为冢，卧者为尸。

translations.literal: Crowd asked cause—Heng said: "Sitters are tombs—liers are corpses.
translations.idiomatic: They asked why; he said, "Seated men are burial mounds; prone men are corpses."

sentences.zh: 尸冢之间，能不悲乎！”

translations.literal: Between corpse and tomb—can one not grieve!
translations.idiomatic: Between tomb and corpse—who would not weep!

sentences.zh: 刘表及荆州士大夫，先服其才名，甚宾礼之，文章言议，非衡不定。

translations.literal: Liu Biao and Jingzhou gentry earlier admired his fame—guest-treated him—writings debate—without Heng unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Biao and the Jingzhou elite already respected his name; they honored him as a guest and let him settle every draft and debate.

sentences.zh: 表尝与诸文人共草章奏，并极其才思。

translations.literal: Biao once with scholars co-drafted memorials—exhausted wit.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Biao once joined scholars drafting memorials and poured out every clever phrase.

sentences.zh: 时衡出，还见之，开省未周，因毁以抵地。

translations.literal: When Heng returned—saw them—opened skimmed not finished—therefore tore and dashed ground.
translations.idiomatic: Mi Heng walked in, skimmed their pile before they finished reading, and tore it to the floor.

sentences.zh: 表怃然为骇。

translations.literal: Biao stunned appalled.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Biao sat thunderstruck.

sentences.zh: 衡乃从求笔札，须臾立成，辞义可观。

translations.literal: Heng asked brush bamboo slips—instant finished—phrasing fine.
translations.idiomatic: Mi Heng demanded ink and slips and in moments produced a polished draft.

sentences.zh: 表大悦，益重之。

translations.literal: Biao greatly pleased—more esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Biao rejoiced and prized him even more.

sentences.zh: 后复侮慢于表，表耻，不能容，以江夏太守黄祖性急，故送衡与之，祖亦善待焉。

translations.literal: Later again insulted Biao—Biao shamed could not bear—because Jiangxia governor Huang Zu quick temper—therefore sent Heng to him—Zu also treated well.
translations.idiomatic: Later Mi Heng insulted Liu Biao again; shamed and unable to endure him, Liu sent him to the short-tempered Jiangxia governor Huang Zu, who still treated him kindly.

sentences.zh: 衡为作书记，轻重疏密，各得体宜。

translations.literal: Heng wrote letters—weight spacing—each apt.
translations.idiomatic: Mi Heng penned Huang Zu's correspondence—every tone and spacing hit the mark.

sentences.zh: 祖持其手曰：“处士，此正得祖意，如祖腹中之所欲言也。”

translations.literal: Zu held his hand: "Retired sir—this hits Zu's mind—as what Zu would say from belly.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zu clasped his hand: "Sir, this is exactly what I meant—words drawn straight from my gut."

sentences.zh: 祖长子射，为章陵太守，尤善于衡。

translations.literal: Zu's eldest son She—Zhangling governor—especially fond of Heng.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zu's eldest son She governed Zhangling and favored Mi Heng above others.

sentences.zh: 嘗與衡俱遊，共讀蔡邕所作碑文，射愛其辭，還恨不繕寫。

translations.literal: Once roamed with Heng—read Cai Yong stele—She loved lines—returned regretted not copied.
translations.idiomatic: They once toured together and read Cai Yong's inscription; She loved the text but regretted having no copy.

sentences.zh: 衡曰：「吾雖一覽，猶能識之，唯其中石缺二字，爲不明耳。」

translations.literal: Heng said: "Though one glance—I remember—only stone lacks two graphs—unclear."
translations.idiomatic: Mi Heng said, "One reading fixes it in memory—only two characters are missing on the stone."

sentences.zh: 因書出之，躬馳使寫碑，還校，如衡所書，莫不嘆伏。

translations.literal: Thereupon he wrote it out; She personally hurried someone to copy the stele, and when he returned and checked it, it was as Heng had written, so none failed to sigh in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Mi Heng wrote the inscription out; Huang She personally sent someone racing back to copy the stele, and when the copy was checked it matched Heng's text exactly, leaving everyone amazed.

sentences.zh: 射時大會賓客，人有獻鸚鵡者，射舉巵於衡曰：「願先生賦之，以娛嘉賓。」

translations.literal: At the time She gathered guests in a great assembly; someone presented a parrot, and She raised a goblet to Heng and said, "I wish, sir, that you compose a fu on it, to delight the honored guests."
translations.idiomatic: At a large banquet, someone presented a parrot. Huang She raised a cup to Mi Heng and said, "Please, sir, compose a fu on it to entertain our guests."

sentences.zh: 衡攬筆而作，文無加點，辭采甚麗。

translations.literal: Heng took up the brush and composed; the writing had no marks added, and its diction and color were very beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: Mi Heng took up the brush and wrote it in one pass, without a single correction; the language was dazzling.

sentences.zh: 後黃祖在蒙衝船上，大會賓客，而衡言不遜順，祖慚，乃呵之。

translations.literal: Later Huang Zu on covered-strike boat—great feast—Heng speech not deferential—Zu shamed—scolded.
translations.idiomatic: Later, aboard a war-boat, Huang Zu feasted guests; Mi Heng spoke harshly, shaming Zu until he snapped.

sentences.zh: 衡更熟视曰：“死公！

translations.literal: Heng stared harder: "Dead old man!
translations.idiomatic: Mi Heng glared: "Corpse of an old official!

sentences.zh: 云等道？”

translations.literal: What sort of talk is this?"
translations.idiomatic: What kind of talk is that?"

sentences.zh: 祖大怒，令五百将出，欲加箠。

translations.literal: Zu furious—ordered guards bring out—meant to whip.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zu roared for guards to drag him out for a beating.

sentences.zh: 衡方大骂，祖恚，遂令杀之。

translations.literal: Heng cursing—Zu enraged—ordered kill.
translations.idiomatic: Mi Heng kept shouting until Zu, furious, ordered him executed.

sentences.zh: 祖主簿素疾衡，即时杀焉。

translations.literal: Zu's registrar always hated Heng—killed at once.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zu's registrar, who long despised Mi Heng, killed him on the spot.

sentences.zh: 射徒跣来救，不及。

translations.literal: She ran barefoot to save—not in time.
translations.idiomatic: She ran barefoot to intervene—too late.

sentences.zh: 祖亦悔之，乃厚加棺敛。

translations.literal: Zu also regretted—rich coffin rites.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Zu repented and buried him with honor.

sentences.zh: 衡时年二十六，其文章多亡云。

translations.literal: Heng age twenty-six—writings mostly lost.
translations.idiomatic: Mi Heng was twenty-six; most of his writings vanished.

sentences.zh: 赞曰：情志既动，篇辞为贵。

translations.literal: Encomium says: emotion stirred—piece's words are treasure.
translations.idiomatic: The summation runs: once feeling moves, the text becomes the prize.

sentences.zh: 抽心呈貌，非雕非蔚。

translations.literal: Draw heart show face—neither carve nor lush excess.
translations.idiomatic: It lays heart bare without carving ornament or piling gloss.

sentences.zh: 殊狀共體，同聲異氣。

translations.literal: Strange forms share one body; the same sound has different breaths.
translations.idiomatic: Many shapes share one body; one tune may carry different breath.

sentences.zh: 言觀麗則，永監淫費。

translations.literal: Strange forms share one body; the same sound has different breaths.
translations.idiomatic: Many shapes share one body; one tune may carry different breath.
